title: RFP – Heating and Cooling System Replacement Design – CCC St John’s
description: Project Description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC), on behalf of Correctional Service Canada (CSC), requires engineering services for the Community Correctional Centre in St. John’s, NL. The project will replace the existing geothermal system with an air-to-water system and address deficiencies in the existing ventilation system. This Request for Proposals (RFP) is issued under Supply Arrangement E0225-150564 for Mechanical and Electrical Engineering Services. The following mechanical firms in Newfoundland and Labrador have been invited: Dillon Consulting, Pageau Morel, and CBCL. Debriefing: Unsuccessful bidders may request a debriefing by contacting the Contracting Authority within fifteen (15) working days of receiving notification. General Information: Proposals must be submitted through SAP Ariba by the date and time specified in the RFP. The issuing office is Atlantic Region Acquisitions, 1713 Bedford Row, Halifax, NS, B3J 1T3. This office provides services in English. Proposals may be submitted in either official language of Canada.

title: Aloittavan yrittäjän neuvontapalvelut
description: Aloittavan yrittäjän neuvontapalvelut 1. Hankinnan kohde Hankinnan kohteena on aloittavien yritysten neuvonta- ja valmennuspalvelukokonaisuus, joka muodostuu kahdesta toisiaan täydentävästä osa-alueesta: 1. yrityksen perustamisneuvonnasta yritystoimintaa suunnitteleville henkilöille sekä 2. yrityksen käynnistämisvaiheen tuesta ja valmennuksesta vastaperustetuille yrityksille. Palvelujen tavoitteena on madaltaa yrittäjäksi ryhtymisen kynnystä, parantaa yritysten toimintaedellytyksiä sekä vahvistaa uusien yritysten elinkelpoisuutta ja jatkuvuutta ensimmäisten toimintavuosien aikana. Palvelukokonaisuuden tulee muodostaa yhtenäinen asiakaspolku liikeidean arvioinnista yrityksen alkuvaiheen kehittämiseen. Tilaajan näkemyksen mukaan palvelu on syytä kilpailuttaa ja tuottaa yhtenä kokonaisuutena, jolloin yritystoimintaa suunnittelevan henkilön ja myöhemmin yrityksen asiakkuus on yhdellä toimijalla. Tällöin palveluntuottaja pystyy parhaalla mahdollisella tavalla tukemaan yritystoimintaa suunnittelevia henkilöitä yrityksen perustamisessa ja vahvistamaan yritysten elinkelpoisuutta ja kasvuedellytyksiä toiminnan alkuvaiheessa. Sopimuskauden aikana Jyväskylässä yritysneuvonta- ja kehittämispalveluita toteutetaan ns. Jyväskylän mallin mukaisesti osana Yritystalo-toimintakonseptia. Yritystalo on yksi yhteinen palvelukeskus, jonka toiminta-ajatuksena on tuoda kaikki kaupungin yritys- ja työnantajapalvelut saman katon alle. 2. Sopimuskausi ja hankinnan arvo Sopimuskausi on 1.1.2027-31.12.2028. Hankintaan sisältyy tilaajan yksipuolinen optio ajalle 1.1.2029-31.12.2029. Hankinnan ennakoitu kokonaisarvo optiokausi mukaan lukien on noin 780 000 euroa (alv 0 %). Tilaaja ei sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin. 3. Palvelun kohderyhmät Palvelut suunnataan erityisesti seuraaville asiakasryhmille: • työttömät työnhakijat • maahanmuuttajat • nuoret • opiskelijat • työssäkäyvät henkilöt • muut yritystoiminnan aloittamista suunnittelevat henkilöt Yrityksen perustamisneuvontaa tarjotaan Jyväskylässä asuville henkilöille. Käynnistämisvaiheen tukea tarjotaan Jyväskylään perustetuille tai pääasiallisesti Jyväskylässä toimiville yrityksille enintään 18 kuukauden ajan yrityksen perustamisesta. 4. Palvelun sisältö 4.1 Yrityksen perustamisneuvonta Palveluntuottajan tulee tarjota yritystoiminnan aloittamista suunnitteleville asiakkaille asiantuntevaa, maksutonta ja puolueetonta neuvontaa. Perustamisneuvonnan tulee sisältää vähintään: • henkilökohtainen yritysneuvonta • ryhmämuotoiset info- ja neuvontatilaisuudet • liikeidean arviointi • yrittäjävalmiuksien arviointi • liiketoimintasuunnitelman laadinnan ohjaus • talous- ja kannattavuuslaskelmien ohjaus • markkina- ja kilpailutilanteen arviointi • yritysmuodon valintaan liittyvä neuvonta • rahoitus-, lupa- ja viranomaisprosesseihin liittyvä ohjaus • yrityksen perustamiseen liittyvä käytännön ohjaus. Palveluntuottajan tulee kyetä palvelemaan asiakkaita suomeksi ja englanniksi. Muiden kielten osalta palveluntuottajan tulee kuvata käytettävät ratkaisut. 4.2 Yrityksen käynnistämisvaiheen tuki ja valmennus Palveluntuottajan tulee tarjota vastaperustetuille yrityksille suunnitelmallista tukea ja valmennusta yrityksen ensimmäisten toimintakuukausien aikana. Tuen tulee perustua mahdollisuuksien mukaan yrityksen perustamisvaiheessa laadittuihin suunnitelmiin, laskelmiin ja kehittämistoimenpiteisiin. Palveluntuottajan tulee varmistaa asiakkuuden saumaton jatkuminen perustamisvaiheesta käynnistämisvaiheen palveluihin. Käynnistämisvaiheen palvelun tulee sisältää vähintään: • yritystoiminnan alkuvaiheen tilannekartoitus • liiketoimintasuunnitelman päivittäminen • myynnin ja markkinoinnin kehittäminen • hinnoittelun ja kannattavuuden seuranta • talouden hallinnan ohjaus • kassavirran hallinnan tuki • digitaalisten työkalujen hyödyntämisen ohjaus • verkostojen ja yhteistyökumppaneiden tunnistaminen • kasvun ja kehittämisen mahdollisuuksien arviointi • yksilöllinen yritysvalmennus. Palvelun tulee olla asiakkaan käytettävissä enintään 18 kuukauden ajan yrityksen perustamisesta. 5. Tavoitteet Tilaajan tavoitteena on, että palvelu: • edistää uusien yritysten syntymistä Jyväskylään • lisää yrittäjyyden houkuttelevuutta eri kohderyhmissä • parantaa yritysten alkuvaiheen menestymismahdollisuuksia • vähentää yritystoiminnan alkuvaiheen keskeytymistä • tukee työllistymistä yrittäjyyden kautta • vahvistaa alueen elinvoimaa. Palveluntuottajan tulee toiminnassaan tavoitella vähintään seuraavan suuruisia palveluvolyymejä: • vähintään 250 uutta perustamisneuvonnan asiakasta vuodessa • vähintään 130 perustamisneuvonnan seurauksena syntyvää yritystä vuodessa. Tilaaja käyttää tavoitteita palvelun vaikuttavuuden arvioinnissa. 6. Palvelun toteuttamistapa Palveluntuottajan tulee järjestää palvelut ensisijaisesti Jyväskylässä. Palveluntuottajan tulee sitoutua tuottamaan palvelua osana Jyväskylän kaupungin Jyväskylän mallin mukaista Yritystalo-konseptia. Palvelua tulee olla saatavilla: • lähitapaamisina • etäpalveluina • puhelin- ja verkkoneuvontana • ryhmätilaisuuksina. Palveluntuottajan tulee huolehtia asiakkaiden yhdenvertaisesta kohtelusta ja palvelujen saavutettavuudesta. 7. Tarjoajan soveltuvuus Tarjoajalla tulee olla: • riittävä kokemus aloittavien yritysten neuvonnasta tai yritysten kehittämispalveluiden tuottamisesta • käytettävissään riittävä määrä yritysneuvonnan asiantuntijoita • osaaminen yrityksen perustamisesta, liiketoiminnan suunnittelusta, yritysrahoituksesta, taloudesta ja yritysten kehittämisestä • valmius tuottaa palvelua monikanavaisesti • asiakasohjausmalli yrittäjän osaamisen vahvistamiseksi Jyväskylän seudun koulutustarjontaa hyödyntäen • dokumentoitu laadunhallintamalli ja vähintään kahden vuoden kokemus ao. laadunhallintamallin toteuttamisesta Tarjoajan soveltuvuutta arvioidaan soveltuvuusvaatimusten ja laatukriteerien perusteella.,

title: Kielotie 28:n toimisto- ja liikerakennuksen purku-urakka
description: Kielotie 28:n toimisto- ja liikerakennuksen purku-urakka Kiinteistö Oy Lehdokkitien Virastotalo pyytää tarjoustanne Kielotie 28:n toimisto- ja liikerakennuksen purku-urakasta kiinteähintaisena kokonaisurakkana tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liiteasiakirjojen mukaisesti. Hankinta toteutetaan avoimella menettelyllä. Purku-urakan kohde on vuonna 1983 valmistunut toimisto- ja liikerakennus, jonka bruttopinta-ala on 6 967 m2. Rakennuksessa on kaksi osaa. Osassa A on neljä kerrosta, kellarikerros sekä osittainen ullakkokerros. Rakennus on perustettu paalujen varaan. Alapohja ja maanvastaiset seinät ovat betonirakenteiset. Rakennuksen runko on paikalla valettu ja se koostuu kantavista ulkoseinistä ja pilaripalkkirungosta. A-osan kellarikerroksessa on sosiaalitiloja, teknisiä tiloja, varastoja ja rakennuksen väestönsuojatilat. B-osa on kolmikerroksinen ja kauttaaltaan nostettu betonipilarien varaan. B-osassa on toimistotiloja kerroksissa 2–4. Väliseinät ovat molemmissa rakennusosissa pääosin muurattuja ja toimistotilojen välillä kevytrakenteisia siirtoseiniä. Rakennuksen vesikattona on bitumikermikatto, sisäpuolisella vedenpoistolla. Rakennuksessa ei ole tehty kattavaa peruskorjausta ja se on pinnoiltaan pääosin alkuperäisessä kunnossa. Kielotie 28:n kortteli on Vantaan kaupunkiympäristön toimialan toimintojen pääasiallisessa käytössä aiemmin ollut toimisto- ja liikerakennus, joka on nyttemmin tyhjentynyt ja poistettu käytöstä. Kaupunkikonsernissa on tehty päätökset kohteen purkamisesta. Kohteen omistaa Kiinteistö Oy Lehdokkitien Virastotalo, jonka osakekannan omistavat yhdessä Vantaan kaupunki ja kaupunkikonserniin kuuluva Vivamus Kiinteistöt Oy. Osakkaat ovat sopineet, että Vivamus Kiinteistöt Oy ohjaa ja koordinoi purku-ukakkaa. Vivamus Kiinteistöt Oy on tehnyt mm. purku-urakassa tarvittavat suunnittelu- ja asiantuntijapalvelusopimukset lukuunsa. Kiinteistö Oy Lehdokkitien Virastotalo pyytää tällä tarjouspyynnöllä tarjouksia kohteen purku-urakasta, jonka tarkempi laajuus ilmenee tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevista asiakirjoista. Urakkapaikan esittelytilaisuudet pidetään paikan päällä 18.11.2026 klo 12.00 ja 19.11.2026 klo 12.00.,

title: Germany – Track construction works – 2. S-Bahn Stammstrecke München, VE833a Bauabschnitt Oberirdisch Ost und Leuchtenbergring
description: Die gegenständliche Vergabe beinhaltet die Bauleistungen für die die Hauptbaumaßnahmen des Bauabschnitts Oberirdisch Ost (BA60) der 2.SBSS. Der BA60 beinhaltet die Anpassung des Spurplans, die durch die Anbindung der neuen Gleise aus dem Tunnel der 2. S-Bahn-Stammstrecke an die bestehenden S-Bahn-Strecken und aus dem Umbau des Bahnhofsteils Leuchtenbergring auf sechs Bahnsteigkanten verursacht wird. Des Weiteren ist das Rampenbauwerk, mit dem die 2. S-Bahn Stammstrecke aus der Tunnellage an die Oberfläche geführt wird, Teil des Bauabschnitts. Der Umbau des Spurplans erfordert die notwendigen Anpassungen des Bahnkörpers, der Entwässerung, des Kabeltiefbaus, des Oberbaus, der Rettungswege sowie von Brücken- und Stützbauwerken an den geänderten Anforderungen. Die bahntechnische Ausrüstung (Oberleitung, Starkstromanlagen, 50 Hz, und TK) ist an den neuen Spurplan angepasst neu zu errichten. In Zusammenhang wird ein Wendegleis östlich vom Leuchtenbergring ergänzt, um die betrieblichen Anforderungen der neuen 2. S-Bahn-Stammstrecke erfüllen zu können und Anpassungsmaßnahmen an der Wendeanlage MOP W zwischen Ostbahnhof und Leuchtenbergring ausgeführt. Das Rampenbauwerk im BA60 beginnt östlich der Berg-am-Laim-Straße als Tunnel in offener bzw. Deckelbauweise und schließt dort direkt an das Querungsbauwerk der Berg-am-Laim-Straße an. Die Blockfuge stellt die Grenze zwischen den Bauabschnitten BA50 (nicht Teil dieser Ausschreibung) und BA60 (Inhalt dieser Ausschreibung) dar. Es besteht aus dem sogenannten Verteilerbauwerk, in dem die zwei Gleise der 2. Stammstrecke mittels Weichen auf 3 Gleise erweitert werden und den drei sogenannten "Finger-Bauwerken", mit denen die 3 Gleise an die Oberfläche geführt werden. Aufgrund der neuen Gleislage werden Anpassungen am Kreuzungsbauwerks km 1,722 der Strecke 5600 und der Eisenbahnüberführung (EÜ) EÜ Berg-am-Laim Straße km 10,469 Strecke 5510 erforderlich, dabei sind bahnsteigartige Anprallschutzkonstruktionen an den Pfeilern zu erstellen. Zudem sind im Zuge der Umgestaltung des Bahnkörpers 5 Stützwände zu errichten. Für den Umbau der bestehenden Station Leuchtenbergring auf sechs Bahnsteigkanten wird ein neuer Bahnsteig 0 nördlich in freier Lage neben dem bestehenden Gleisfeld errichtet. Der Bahnsteig liegt teilweise über der bestehenden EÜ Leuchtenbergring, aus der Bahnsteigzugänge jeweils vom westlichen und östlichen Gehweg der Leuchtenbergring-Unterführung hergestellt werden. Die EÜ Leuchtenbergring wird durch eine zu errichtende Bahnsteigträgerkonstruktion überspannt. Außerdem werden die Bestandsbahnsteige A und B komplett erneuert, der Bahnsteig A in etwa in Bestandslage, der Bahnsteig B wird nach Osten verlegt. Die vorhandenen Treppenabgänge zur Leuchtenbergring Unterführung werden wie im Bestand beibehalten. In Zusammenhang mit dem Umbau der Bahnsteige wird durch die Landeshauptstadt München ein Fußgängersteg errichtet, der ebenfalls Teil dieser Vergabe ist. Dieser Steg befindet sich westlich der Bahnsteige 0, A und B und überspannt das Gleisfeld von Nord nach Süd. Der Steg wird durch Festtreppen und Aufzüge an die 3 Bahnsteige angeschlossen und gewährleistet einen barrierefreien Zugang zur Verkehrsstation Leuchtenbergring. Die gegenständliche Vergabe beinhaltet die Bauleistungen der genannten Gewerke sowie die Leistungen zur Ausführungsplanung für Baubehelfe. Auszug aus dem Umfang der Leistungen: Verteiler- und Rampenbauwerk ca. 6000 m² Grundfläche in Deckel- und offener Bauweise Gleisbau: ca. 70 Weichen, ca. 9000 m Gleisbau Bahnsteige: ca. 630 m Mittelbahnsteige STEG LHM

title: J065--Imaging Service & Maintenance EHCC & MTV
description: This is for preventative maintenance and service of Philips Imaging equipment. See the solicitation that follows for full details and requirements. SERVICES TO BE PROVIDED: A. Repairs Service Hours:� All repairs will be performed during normal VA business hours (8:00 AM 4:30 PM, Monday-Friday), excluding Federal Holidays unless otherwise specified. Contractor may work outside normal business hours by arrangement with the COR if such services are provided without additional charge to the government. Any overtime charges must be approved by the COR or designee prior to the initiation of overtime work. Response Time:� A technical support representative will respond by telephone to the VA within thirty (30) minutes of the original service call. The contractor will arrive on-site for repair within four (4) hours of the original service call. Radiology equipment shall have a guaranteed uptime of 97% or greater. Ultrasound Equipment shall have an uptime of 95% or greater, ensuring minimal downtime for critical diagnostic operations. Documentation and Resources:� The VA shall not provide service manuals or service diagnostic software to the contractor. The contractor shall obtain, have on file, and make available to its FSE(s) all operational and technical documentation (e.g., operational and service manuals, schematics, parts lists) necessary to meet the performance requirements of this contract. The location and listing of the service data manuals, by name, and/or the manuals shall be provided to the CO upon request. Any charges for parts, manuals, tools, or necessary software for maintenance/repairs are included within this contract and its agreed-upon price unless otherwise stated in writing. B. Parts Replacement Parts:� The contractor shall provide all necessary replacement parts to ensure the equipment performs within the manufacturer's specifications. This includes, but is not limited to, coverage for tubes, ultrasound probes, detectors, grids, tables, and batteries. All replacement parts must meet or exceed the factory specifications to maintain compatibility with existing systems and support future performance and reliability upgrades. Any parts removed and replaced by the contractor will become the property of the contractor. Replaced parts must be delivered on-site no later than 10:30 AM the following day. C. Software Updates/Upgrades Software Maintenance:� The contractor will furnish, free of charge, all OEM software or hardware upgrades to the equipment purchased by the VA, which are intended to correct safety risks. Software updates offering enhancements to previously purchased software features shall also be covered under this service agreement if they do not require hardware modifications or additions. D. Scheduled Maintenance Preventive Maintenance (PM):� The contract will include comprehensive scheduled preventive maintenance inspections (PM) as required by manufacturer specifications. Scheduling:� A mutually agreeable time for the inspections will be scheduled through the COR, Healthcare Technology Management (HTM) staff, or the Radiology supervisor/CT Lead. Inspection and Maintenance Procedures:� The contractor will perform PM Services to ensure that equipment listed above functions in conformance with the latest published editions of NFPA-99, OSHA, and CDRH standards. The contractor shall provide and utilize procedures and checklists with worksheet originals indicating work performed and actual values obtained (as applicable) provided to the COR or HTM staff upon completion of the PM. Preventive maintenance procedures will be submitted to the COR for approval prior to initiation of this service and kept on file. PM services shall include, but are not limited to: Cleaning of equipment Reviewing operating system diagnostics to ensure system operation meets manufacturer's specifications Calibrating and lubricating the equipment Performing non-emergent remedial maintenance Testing and replacing faulty or worn parts and/or parts likely to become faulty, fail, or become worn Inspecting and replacing necessary cables and bushings Measuring, adjusting, and calibrating for optimal image quality Inspecting all mechanical components including, but not limited to, probes, cables, mounting hardware, chains, belts, bearings, tracks, interlocks, clutches, motors, monitors, keyboards for mechanical integrity, safety, performance Returning equipment to full and proper operating condition per manufacturer specifications Conducting an electrical safety inspection (as applicable) and documenting the results. Compliance:� The contractor, their personnel, and their subcontractors shall be subject to Federal laws, regulations, standards, and VA Directives and Handbooks regarding information and information system security as delineated in this contract.

title: Professional Travel Agency Services

title: Roadside Vegetation Brushing 2026 - Highway Operations Unit
description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to bid solicitations is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency (PCA) has a requirement for a contractor to provide roadside vegetation management, brushing, clearing, and isolated tree removal services along designated sections of the Trans-Canada Highway in Yoho National Park (approximately 9 km), Highway 93 North in Banff National Park (approximately 19 km), and Highway 93 North in Jasper National Park (approximately 5 km). The work includes the removal and control of grass, brush, shrubs, small trees, and other vegetation within specified highway rights-of-way to improve highway safety by maintain sightlines, protect road infrastructure. and reduce hazards, in accordance with Parks Canada environmental, operational, and traffic management requirements. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI04 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor shall perform and complete the Work no later than March 31, 2027. OPTIONAL SITE VISIT It is recommended that the Bidder or a representative of the Bidder visit the work site. Arrangements have been made for the site visit to be held at Niblock Pit Gate on HWY 93N (https://maps.app.goo.gl/jYrHNdeHmVudrEqXA) on novembre 24, 2026. The site visit will begin 10:00AM (MDT-HAR). Bidders should communicate with the Contracting Authority no later than novembre 23, 2026, at 11:00AM (MDT-HAR). to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders must also complete and submit a certification. Bidders who do not confirm attendance, provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend, or who do not complete and submit the above certification as required will not be allowed access to the site. Bidders will be requested to sign an attendance sheet. No alternative appointment will be given to bidders who do not attend or do not send a representative. Bidders who do not participate in the visit will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: Tender for contract: Database with general and financial data of corporates and countries on a global scale
description: EIFO wishes to procure access to a global database containing company, financial and credit information to support EIFO's credit assessment and case management activities. The database shall provide coverage of companies on a global scale, including Ukraine and other high-risk countries. The service shall, to the extent available for the individual company and jurisdiction, provide access to: - Company identification and general corporate information; - Ownership information, including shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners and corporate group structures; - Information on management, board members and authorised representatives; - Financial statements, historical financial information and key financial figures; - Credit ratings and other relevant credit information; and - Payment behaviour, negative credit information and other information relevant to the assessment of a company's creditworthiness. The solution shall be accessible through a web-based user interface and shall support report export/download. EIFO expects approximately 50 users and an annual volume of approximately 1000 unique companies. The contract will be concluded for a period of 24 months with an option for EIFO to extend the contract once for a further period of 12 months.

title: Z1DA--NRM CONST - 528A7-18-707 - Replace Boiler Stack Rome CBOC
description: CONTINUATION OF SF 30 BLOCK 14 AMENDMENT DESCRIPTION 0002 AGAINST SOLICITATION NO. 36C24227R0008 1. This amendment answers the following vendor questions: Number of boiler vents: On M-101 (Boiler and Generator Exhaust Plan, Phase II), the new wall penetration/chase is labeled with two 14" I.D. pipes and one 12" I.D. pipe. Keynote 2 calls for a single "new 14" boiler double walled insulated vent stack," and the cutover notes describe that one vent connecting to Boiler #1 and continuing to within two feet of Boiler #2's vent, so one common 14" vent appears to serve both boilers. The solicitation description, however, refers to "two new steel boiler exhaust stacks." Please confirm whether the work is: (a) one 14" double-wall vent common to Boiler #1 and Boiler #2, plus the 12" generator exhaust, or (b) two separate 14" double-wall vents (one per boiler), plus the 12" generator exhaust. If (a), please confirm what the second 14" pipe shown at the penetration represents. Answer: Confirming: it is (b) two separate 14" double-wall vents (one per boiler), plus the 12" generator exhaust. b) Draft control or stack fan: No stack fan, draft inducer, or boiler-outlet draft control appears on the drawings. Section 23 51 00 (paragraph 2.2, Boiler Outlet Dampers and Accessories) refers to automatic draft control specified in Section 23 09 11, but Section 23 09 11 is not included in the solicitation. Please confirm whether: (a) the new boiler vent is intended to operate on natural draft (no fan or draft control required), or (b) a mechanical draft fan and/or barometric or motorized draft control is expected. If so, please issue Section 23 09 11 or identify the required equipment and control sequence. Answer: Confirming: it is (a) the new boiler vent is intended to operate on natural draft (no fan or draft control required). c) Design heating load and operating water temperatures: Please provide the building design heating load (or recent gas and oil usage or meter data), and the normal heating-water supply and return temperatures for the two existing Fulton Vantage boilers. Return-water temperature sets the flue-gas temperature, which governs the vent sizing and draft calculation. Please also confirm whether the two boilers operate as lead/standby (N+1) or are both required at design load. Answer: Replacing the boiler is not part of the contract. Boilers have inducer fans. There is no stack fan or boiler draft controls to be installed. d) Facility designation: Please confirm whether the Rome CBOC is designated mission-critical under VA Physical Security and Resiliency Design requirements, or otherwise required to keep heating on during a utility outage, as this affects the vent design for both fuels. Answer: Rome CBOC is NOT designated as a Critical/Mission Critical facility. CBOCs are generally outpatient facilities rather than hospitals with inpatient, emergency, surgical, or continuity-of-government functions. Therefore, absent a specific VA risk assessment or designation, the Rome CBOC would not ordinarily be assumed to be mission critical. e) Fuel oil and emergency power: Boiler #2 fires #2 fuel oil as a backup fuel. Please confirm (a) whether the vent must be designed for oil firing on Boiler #2 (and on Boiler #1, if applicable), (b) the size and required reserve of the existing #2 oil tank, and (c) whether the boilers and their associated vent or draft equipment are served by emergency power through an automatic transfer switch. Answer: The specified vent material (AL-29-4C) is compatible for operating the boilers on natural gas or #2 oil. This contract does not include altering the existing fuel oil tank, day tank, the boilers, or the generator. We are eliminating the existing exhaust stack and installing a new exhaust stack in a different location to serve the two existing boilers and existing emergency generator. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged.

title: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Request for Information (RFI) - provide canines to the CBP Field Office K9 (FOK9) and Border Patrol K9 (BPK9) training centers.
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This is an RFI released pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 5 (Presolicitation & Early Industry Exchanges) & Part 12 (Commercial Streamlining). This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) nor a promise to issue an RFP or other solicitation. Furthermore, those who respond to this RFI should not anticipate feedback about its submission, other than acknowledgment of receipt. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is not currently seeking proposals. Respondents are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay any cost incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the expense of the respondent. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. All submissions become the property of the Federal Government and will not be returned. The requirements outlined in this RFI and its attachments do not represent definitive CBP requirements and are subject to change prior to any potential future solicitation. Vendors should not interpret the listed requirements as final or representative of CBP's actual requirements. The listed requirements are for informational purposes only and are covered in attachment #1. This purpose of this RFI is to gather market research information for acquisition planning purposes in anticipation of issuing a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) to provide canines to the Field Office K9 (FOK9) and Border Patrol K9 (BPK9) training centers. Goal is to obtain industry comments relating to the attached draft Statement of Work (SOW). Responses will assist CBP in developing and refining its Acquisition Strategy, Statement of Work, and Performance Specifications in developing the anticipated BPA. Relevant to this RFI, please include the following suggested information. Company Information Legal business name, address, website, and primary point of contact. Business size and socioeconomic designations, if applicable. UEI code. Primary NAICS code Relevant Experience Include examples of recent, relevant contracts. For each example include: contract number if with CBP Customer or agency if not with CBP Relevance to this RFI Limit the comments to two pages. Use a clear, professional format with readable headings and standard fonts. Limit comments to about the attached SOW. This is not an RFP, do not include any pricing information. Responses on this RFI must be sent via email to the following: CBP Procurement POC: Danielle Brandao Lacerda, Contract Specialist at DANIELLE.BRANDAOLACERDA@cbp.dhs.gov and John Crockett, Contracting Officer, at JOHN.T.CROCKETT@cbp.dhs.gov RFI responses must be electronically submitted to the procurement POC by 12:00 pm EDT on December 2nd, 2026. Include the RFI title in the subject line of your email. See Attachment 1, Draft Statement of Work.

DESCRIPTION This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The solicitation number is 36C24927Q0014. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Quotations (RFQ) for commercial services. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2025-03, effective January 17, 2025, as well as applicable VAAR deviations, VA Acquisition Manual guidance, and VA policy updates in effect on the date of solicitation issuance. This acquisition is set aside exclusively for 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) concerns. The applicable NAICS code is 561990, All Other Support Services, with a small business size standard of $16.5 million. The Government intends to issue a purchase order or contract to the responsible offeror whose quotation conforms to the requirements of this solicitation and is determined to provide the best value to the Government in accordance with the evaluation procedures stated herein. This acquisition will be conducted pursuant to the authority of FAR Part 13, Simplified Acquisition Procedures. 5. APPLICABLE REGULATIONS AND CONTRACT CLAUSES This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses in effect through the applicable Federal Acquisition Circular, including FAR provisions and clauses applicable to commercial services, as well as the current Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) and Department of Veterans Affairs acquisition policies and deviations. The solicitation will incorporate, as applicable: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) provisions and clauses; Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) provisions and clauses; Applicable FAR and VAAR deviations, including: FAR 52.212-5, as modified by the February 2025 deviation; Applicable VAAR deviations and updates; Applicable VA Acquisition Manual (VAAM) guidance; and Applicable VA policy alerts and policy flashes. Provisions and clauses incorporated by reference have the same force and effect as if they were provided in full text. The full text of FAR provisions and clauses is available at: https://www.acquisition.gov/far/ The full text of VAAR provisions and clauses is available at: https://www.va.gov/oal/library/vaar/ 6. REQUIREMENT The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, transportation, supervision, and other resources necessary to perform secure document shredding and destruction services for Tennessee Valley Healthcare Services and all associated locations identified in the SOW. Services shall include the collection, transportation, shredding, destruction, and appropriate documentation of Government records and other materials designated for destruction. All services shall be performed in accordance with the requirements of the SOW and applicable Federal, state, and local laws and regulations. Delivery and service locations are identified in the SOW and include Tennessee Valley Healthcare Services and all properties included therein. 7. LINE ITEMS AND PRICING Offerors shall provide pricing for all line items and contract periods identified below. The Government may revise the line-item structure before issuance to conform to the final pricing schedule and Statement of Work. Offerors may use their own pricing format provided that pricing is sufficiently 8. INSTRUCTIONS FOR SUBMISSION OF QUOTES Offerors shall submit a complete quotation by the date and time specified above. An offeror may submit its own pricing document; however, the pricing must be sufficiently detailed and broken out by contract period, location, service, frequency, and any other applicable cost element to permit the Government to conduct a price reasonableness determination. Quotes shall also include documentation demonstrating the offeror s eligibility as a certified SDVOSB, as applicable, and any other information required by the SOW or solicitation provisions. 9. description: DRAFT - Solicitation 36C24927Q0014, Amendment 0003 ATTACHMENT 1 LIMITATIONS ON SUBCONTRACTING PERFORMANCE APPROACH Solicitation 36C24927Q0014 - Amendment 0003 This attachment is incorporated into and made a part of RFQ 36C24927Q0014 by Amendment 0003. 1. Purpose Each quoter shall submit a concise narrative explaining its anticipated approach to performing the requirement and complying with VAAR 852.219-75, VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting - Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction. The Government will use the narrative to evaluate the quoter's understanding and the reasonableness of its proposed technical approach. 2. Applicable Limitation This acquisition is for services, except construction. The contractor shall not pay more than 50 percent of the amount paid by the Government to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs or certified VOSBs, subject to the terms, exclusions, and treatment of similarly situated entities stated in VAAR 852.219-75 and 13 CFR 125.6. 3. Required Submission Submit a document titled 'Limitations on Subcontracting Performance Approach.' The narrative should be sufficiently detailed to permit evaluation but should not include proprietary information beyond what is necessary to explain the proposed approach. A recommended length is five pages, excluding the signed VAAR certification and supporting tables. At a minimum, address the following: Element Required Information Performance approach Identify the principal work elements, the work the prime expects to perform, and the work it expects to subcontract. Anticipated subcontracting Identify anticipated subcontractors, if known; describe their expected work; and provide estimated dollar values or percentages. Identify whether each subcontractor is expected to qualify as a similarly situated entity. Compliance calculation Provide a reasonable illustrative calculation showing the anticipated amount paid by the Government, amounts expected to be paid to non-certified firms, amounts attributed to similarly situated entities, and any proposed exclusions permitted by the governing requirements. Monitoring and controls Describe how the contractor will monitor invoices, payments, lower-tier subcontracting, certification status, and changes affecting compliance during each period of performance. Corrective action Describe how potential noncompliance will be identified, elevated, corrected, documented, and reported to the Contracting Officer when required. Consistency Ensure the narrative is consistent with the technical and price quotation, including the proposed labor, equipment, vehicles, facilities, and subcontracting approach. 4. Separate Mandatory Certification The quoter shall also complete, sign, and submit the certification contained in VAAR 852.219-75(d). The performance-approach narrative does not substitute for the clause certification. The Government will not consider a quotation for award if the required certification is not submitted, as stated in VAAR 852.219-75(d). 5. Evaluation Under the Technical factor, the Government will evaluate whether the submission demonstrates an understanding of the limitations on subcontracting and presents a reasonable, internally consistent approach to maintaining compliance during performance. The Government may consider the relationship among the performance approach, proposed subcontracting, price quotation, resources, and other technical information. The performance approach is not a substitute for an SBA status determination and will not be used to impose a requirement more restrictive than VAAR 852.219-75, 13 CFR 125.6, or other applicable law. A deficient narrative may lower the Government's assessment of the quotation under the Technical factor. The mandatory effect of failing to submit the signed VAAR 852.219-75(d) certification remains governed by the clause. 6. Post-Award Compliance The contractor remains responsible for actual compliance throughout performance. Consistent with VAAR 852.219-75(b) and (c), the Contracting Officer may request records needed to assess compliance, including invoices, subcontracts, payment records, lower-tier information, and calculations. Any performance approach incorporated into the award will supplement, but will not supersede, the clause or applicable law. 7. Revised Addendum to FAR 52.212-1 Add the following to the quotation submission requirements: 'Limitations on Subcontracting Performance Approach required by Amendment 0003, together with the separately completed and signed VAAR 852.219-75(d) Certificate of Compliance.' 8. Revised Section E.2 Technical Factor Add the following technical evaluation element: 'The Government will evaluate the quoter's understanding of and reasonable approach to complying with VAAR 852.219-75, including the relationship between work performed by the prime, work subcontracted to similarly situated entities, work subcontracted to other firms, monitoring controls, and consistency with the technical and price quotation.' description: The Huntington District Corps of Engineers intends to procure an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract for Mowing and Maintenance Services for Burnsville Lake, Burnsville, WV. The contract will be a Firm Fixed Price, Commercial Service type contract with a ceiling amount of $1,100,000.00 over the entire contract period. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. Evaluation Factor A (Past Performance), Factor B (Management and Controls), Factor C (Equipment/Personnel), and Factor D (Cost/Price) are listed in descending order of importance. The best value tradeoff process will be used in this acquisition with award made (as a whole) to the offeror whose quote conforms to the solicitation and has been evaluated as most advantageous to the Government with appropriate consideration given to the evaluation factors. Offerors will be cautioned that the award may not necessarily be made to the lowest price offered. All non-priced factors, when combined, are more important than price. In accordance with 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (DEVIATION), by submission of an offer and execution of a contract, the Contractor agrees to comply with the limitations on subcontracting. To demonstrate compliance, the contractor shall submit the Post-Award Contractors Limitations on Subcontracting Certification to the Contracting Officer or Contracting Officers Representative (COR) if one has been appointed. For contracts with a period of performance lasting less than 12 months, the contractor shall submit the Certification at the end of the performance period. For contracts with a period of performance lasting more than 12 months, the contractor shall submit the Certification at the one-year anniversary of contract award and then annually thereafter until the end of the performance period. For contracts with options years, the contractor shall submit the Certification at the end of the base year and then at the end of each subsequent option year. Solicitation documents will be available on or about 09 November 2026, online at https://www.piee.eb.mil. To be eligible for contract award, an Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Register via the SAM website at https://www.sam.gov. Questions may be submitted to Tatum Bock at tatum.a.bock@usace.army.mil . A NAICS Code of 561730 has been established for this solicitation. The size standard is $9,500,000 in average annual receipts. This procurement is 100% Small Business set-aside.

Title of Requirement Military type litters, stands and carts Background The Veterans Health Administration Office of Emergency Management supports Federal patient movement responsibilities under the National Disaster Medical System and the Department of Defense contingency mission. VHA maintains forty-eight Federal Coordinating Centers located across major cities in the United States and Puerto Rico, and those sites require standardized cache equipment to support reception, triage, and patient placement during disasters, exercises, and contingency operations. Required Equipment and Minimum Salient Characteristics The contractor shall furnish the following items or equal products that meet or exceed the minimum characteristics listed below. 1. Standard Folding Litter, Decontaminable, Rigid Pole NSN 6530-01-380-7309. Part #s multiple vendors 1-00047, 80760, 100047, MIL-L-16462, 100047 and 93-0010 Standard patient litter compatible with litter-mounting equipment used in medical evacuation vehicles and aircraft. Polypropylene cover. Aluminum poles and nylon handles. Adjustable overall length from 90 inches to at least 94.4 inches; nominal length 91.6 inches. 2. Oversized Litter (OSL) NSN 6530-01-552-7708. Part #s 60-0023, 6530NCM071439, 3459 Certified safe-to-fly by the U.S. Air Force and listed, or eligible for listing, on the applicable Safe-to-Fly approval list. Flame-retardant Nomex/Kevlar-blend fabric cover. Six stirrups. Bi-fold configuration with additional carrying loops. Minimum of six IV attachment points. Minimum of three patient securing straps. 3. Litter Stands (Set of 2) 33 Inch NSN 6530-01-523-3314. Part # 6530NCM041094, 04-1229, 60-0014, or STN-FIX Compatible with Talon, Raven, T3, and Mede c litters. Aluminum structure. Minimum capacity of 1,200 pounds. 4. Oversized Litter Stands (Set of 3) Part # 60-0029 Aluminum structure. Extended height of approximately 32 inches. Minimum capacity of 1,600 pounds. 5. EL3000 NATO Wheeled Litter Carrier Part # 6530NCM115921, 21881, 2221030, or 9636 NSN 6530-01-591-9636. Open dimensions approximately 158 cm x 62 cm x 86 cm. Closed dimensions approximately 52 cm x 62 cm x 84 cm. Powder-coated steel with cataphoresis paint process. Stainless steel fittings. Minimum capacity of 500 pounds. This item is identified in the draft as supported by a separate sole source justification within the acquisition package. 6. EL2000 and EL3000 XL Bariatric Transport Cart Green color. Open dimensions approximately 158 cm x 74 cm x 86 cm. Closed dimensions approximately 52 cm x 74 cm x 84 cm. Powder-coated steel with cataphoresis paint process. Stainless steel fittings. Minimum capacity of 600 pounds. 7. Bariatric Wheelchair Minimum capacity of 700 pounds. Seat dimensions approximately 24 inches by 18 inches. Adjustable seat height from 17.5 inches to 19.5 inches. Conventional desk-length arms. Two swing-away footrests per chair. Warranty The contractor shall provide written warranty information for all delivered items, including coverage terms, duration, and procedures for repair or replacement. title: Long-Term Pavement Performance (LTPP) Program Engineering Services Contract (LPES)
description: This Synopsis is issued in accordance with FAR Part 5.203 in response to the mandatory requirement for a 15-day pre-solicitation notification. The purpose of this Synopsis is to announce the Federal Highway Administration�s (FHWA) intent to issue a solicitation for a Full and Open Competition to provide highly specialized engineering services, including field survey operations, data quality management, scientific data curation, and technology transfer support services for the LTPP program and related highway infrastructure research initiatives. FHWA contemplates award of one or more Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity contracts to successfully carry out the technical support services detailed in the Statement of Work (SOW). Offerors must demonstrate technical capability in at least one (1) Task Area to be eligible for a Base ID/IQ contract award. The anticipated period of performance shall not exceed 60 months for the ID/IQ contracts. This Synopsis is issued in accordance with FAR Part 5.203 in response to the mandatory requirement for a 15-day pre-solicitation notification. The purpose of this Synopsis is to announce the Federal Highway Administration�s (FHWA) intent to issue a solicitation for a Full and Open Competition to provide highly specialized engineering services, including field survey operations, data quality management, scientific data curation, and technology transfer support services for the LTPP program and related highway infrastructure research initiatives. FHWA contemplates award of one or more Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity contracts to successfully carry out the technical support services detailed in the Statement of Work (SOW). Offerors must demonstrate technical capability in at least one (1) Task Area to be eligible for a Base ID/IQ contract award. The anticipated period of performance shall not exceed 60 months for the ID/IQ contracts. The main objective of this contract is to provide highly specialized engineering services, including field survey operations, data quality management, scientific data curation, and technology transfer support services for the LTPP program and related highway infrastructure research initiatives. This requirement demands comprehensive technical expertise spanning pavement, bridge, and other highway infrastructure engineering, as well as advanced data systems: Specifically, the LPES contract vehicle is structured to achieve the following overarching strategic objectives: Execute comprehensive pavement condition data collection, incorporating high-speed 3D surface condition profiling (3D APCS), continuous traffic-speed deflection testing, under a rigorous Data Quality Management Plan (DQMP) to ensure defensible and research-grade data quality. Formulate strategic pavement research plans advancing the LTPP program, conduct targeted performance case studies, and deliver practical engineering tools, Section 508-compliant publications, and technical webinars. Develop and curate specialized, analysis-ready datasets for machine learning (ML) and predictive modeling across LTPP and broader highway infrastructure domains, integrating modern database architectures and coordinating data schemas with web portal contractors for public release. To fulfill the LTPP program mission and support broader FHWA pavement and other infrastructure research, the scope of work is organized across three (3) primary Task Areas. Contractors are not required to perform across all Task Areas unless awarded task orders in those areas: Task Area A � Data Collection and Processing: The Contractor shall provide all labor, contractor-owned survey vehicles, specialized diagnostic equipment, materials, and traffic control services necessary to perform automated high-speed 3D surface condition profiling, as well as deflection testing using the Traffic-Speed Deflection Device (TSDD) and Falling Weight Deflectometer (FWD) methods. Work also includes executing a comprehensive Data Quality Management Plan (DQMP), performing ground-truth equipment calibrations, field validations, and routine sensor verifications, conducting relational database processing, and delivering verified data for public portal ingestion. Task Area B � Pavement Performance Data Analysis and Product Development: The Contractor shall perform pavement research analytics, review and execute strategic pavement data analysis plans, conduct targeted pavement performance case studies, and advance and validate state-of-the art pavement testing technologies. Work also includes developing user-friendly web-based engineering tools for State DOT practitioners, publishing 508-compliant documents and facilitating regional practitioner workshops for technology transfer. Task Area C � Special Research Datasets Development: The Contractor shall develop, update, and curate specialized research datasets for broader highway infrastructure research applications. Work includes establishing automated ingestion pipelines and designing modern database schemas to process, quality-check, and store high-resolution 3D Automated Pavement Condition Survey (3D APCS) and continuous deflection datasets; engineering and refining automated data pipelines to produce clean, reliable, and optimized datasets, machine learning feature stores, and structured data environments to support advanced computational modeling across FHWA InfoHighway platforms; generating, validating, developing, and updating computed parameters required for mechanistic-empirical pavement design and machine learning models; and executing close technical coordination with external InfoHighway web portal support contractors (responsible for web portal administration and hosting) to align data schemas, resolve technical issues, provide technical support to data users and stakeholders, and ensure seamless dataset delivery for public releases and web portal data deployments.

description: ISBEE Set-Aside � 24/7 Telebehavioral Health Emergency Department Support Services Solicitation No. 75H70627R00006 This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12, as supplemented by the attached solicitation documents. This announcement and its attachments constitute the solicitation. Proposals are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation No. 75H70627R00006 is issued as a Request for Proposals (RFP) for 24/7 Telebehavioral Health Emergency Department Support Services. The Great Plains Area Indian Health Service (IHS) seeks a contractor to provide non-personal, synchronous audio-video telebehavioral health services 24 hours per day, seven days per week, including weekends and federal holidays. Initial supported Emergency Departments are Pine Ridge, Rosebud, and Eagle Butte in South Dakota, and Fort Yates and Belcourt in North Dakota. Services include crisis behavioral health assessment, suicide-risk evaluation, safety planning, crisis intervention, placement assistance, interpreter-access coordination, and medication-stabilization consultation by qualified prescribing providers when clinically indicated. The contractor shall furnish qualified licensed personnel, staffing management, backup and surge coverage, credentialing support, and other contractor-furnished resources necessary to perform the Performance Work Statement (PWS) and applicable task orders. This acquisition is set aside exclusively for Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs). The assigned NAICS code is 621112, Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists, with a small business size standard of $13.5 million. Offerors shall satisfy the eligibility and representation requirements in the solicitation and submit the completed IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form with their proposals. The anticipated award is a firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with one 12-month base ordering period and four 12-month option ordering periods. The anticipated start date for services is August 1, 2027. The anticipated base period is August 1, 2027, through July 31, 2028, with an ordering period extending through July 31, 2032, if all options are exercised. Services will be authorized and funded through written task orders identifying covered facilities, performance periods, and applicable requirements. The contract minimum guarantee is $25,000, and the maximum ordering ceiling is $2,600,000. The ceiling does not represent guaranteed expenditures or orders beyond the contract minimum. Section F of the attached solicitation identifies the CLINs, service descriptions, quantities, units of measure, and performance periods. Offerors shall complete that price schedule with firm-fixed monthly pricing by facility for the base period and each option period. The total evaluated price will include the base period and all four option periods. Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal conforms to the solicitation and represents the best value to the Government. Evaluation factors are Technical Capability, Past Performance, Management Approach, and Price. When combined, the non-price factors are significantly more important than price. The Government intends to award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussions as provided in the solicitation. Questions must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) Central Standard Time (CST) on November 18, 2026. Proposals must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) CST on December 2, 2026. Submit questions and proposals electronically to David.Jones@ihs.gov, referencing Solicitation No. 75H70627R00006 in the email subject line. Offerors must have a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and active SAM.gov registration as required by the solicitation. Applicable solicitation provisions and contract clauses are identified in the attached provision/clause schedule. Incorporated FAR provisions and clauses are accessible at https://www.acquisition.gov. Review the complete attached solicitation package, including the PWS, price schedule, submission instructions, evaluation criteria, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, and any amendments before submitting a proposal.

title: Z2DA--FY27 EHRM | 657-21-702JC EHRM Training And Administrative Space Construction - St Louis John Cochran
description: INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting bids and subsequently awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract for the design-bid-build EHRM Training and Administrative Space Construction project at the St. Louis VA Health Care System (VAHCS) John Cochran campus located at 915 North Grand BLVD, St. Louis, MO 63106. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The VA Saint Louis Health Care System John Cochran Division requires a construction contractor to perform upgrades in support of the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) program. The construction area is located on the first floor of Building 2 and includes both training and administrative spaces. This project includes the execution of Phases 2, 3, and 4 of the associated design plans. Phase 2 addresses the North Training Rooms (Rooms 139, 140, 141, 142), totaling approximately 2,000 square feet. Work includes upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes. Phase 3 addresses the South Training Rooms (Rooms 126, 127, 128), totaling approximately 1,800 square feet. Work includes upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes. Additionally, Phase 3 includes the renovation of a 130-square-foot breakroom, with new floor and wall finishes, casework, a new sink, and a cold-water tie-in for an ice machine. Phase 4 addresses multiple areas: renovation of an approximately 1,400-square-foot corridor with new floor and wall finishes; upgrades to two offices (approximately 150 square feet each) with upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes; and upgrades to an existing data closet, including new floor and wall finishes, installation of an additional server rack with associated equipment, and replacement of the existing mini-split HVAC unit. Note: Phase 1 is excluded from this scope, as it was completed under a separate contract. Note: All power and data drops originally indicated as floor-mounted shall now be wall-mounted, as shown on revised drawings EP101 and TN101. Installation must match these updated sheet details; no floor-mounted outlets are permitted. ADMINISTRATIVE The solicitation will be issued as an Invitation for Bids (IFB) conducted in accordance with FAR part 14 and will be evaluated in accordance with the procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45.0 million. The solicitation will be issued in early to mid-October 2026. The period of performance is approximately 150 calendar days from the issuance of the notice to proceed. title: Armed Security Guard services
description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Center for Domestic Preparedness (CDP), requires Armed Security Guard Services as described in the attached Statement of Work (SOW) 1 This RFI has been developed to solicit market research information from industry. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. It is not a Request for Proposal, a Request for Quotation, an Invitation for Bids, a Solicitation, or an indication the CDP will contract for the items contained in the RFI. This RFI is part of a Government market research effort to determine the scope of industry capabilities and interest and will be treated as information only. In accordance with RFO FAR 15.201(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responses to this RFI are strictly voluntary and the Government will not pay respondents for information provided in response to this RFI. Responses to this RFI will not be returned and respondents will not be notified of the result of the review. If a Solicitation is issued, it will be announced on Contract Opportunities (available at: https://sam.gov/content/opportunities), at a later date, and all interested parties must respond to that Solicitation announcement separately from any response to this announcement. This RFI does not restrict the Government's acquisition approach on any future Solicitation. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION AND DISCLAIMERS: Respondents shall identify any proprietary information in their RFI response. Information submitted in response to this RFI will be used at the discretion of the Government. Further, the information submitted will remain confidential insofar as permitted by law, including the Freedom of Information and Privacy Act. FEMA reserves the right to utilize any non-proprietary technical information in the anticipated PWS or solicitation. Although it is not necessary to address in their response, respondents shall be aware of any potential, actual, or perceived organizational conflicts of interest. Any real or potential conflicts must be sufficiently mitigated prior to a contract award. For further guidance, refer to the RFO FAR Part 9.5. NO PROPOSALS ARE BEING REQUESTED OR ACCEPTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS SYNOPSIS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED AS A RESULT OF THIS RFI. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this RFI or any follow-up information requests. The purpose of this RFI is to identify sources, collect information on socio-economic status and receive industry comments on the draft Statement of Work (SOW) including (but not limited to) technical questions and comments, contract pricing considerations and contract type for the competitively contracted services for Armed Security Guard Services for the Center for Domestic Preparedness in Anniston, Alabama. The CDP is a national training facility located in Anniston, Alabama that prepares state and local emergency response personnel to respond to all-hazards, including terrorist attacks using weapons of mass destruction, by providing advanced, hands-on training. This national training program was developed for state, local, tribal, Federal, private sector and international responders from Fire Service, Law Enforcement, Emergency Medical Services, Emergency Management, HazMat, Public Health, Healthcare, Public Communications, Public Works and Government Administrative and other emergency response personnel, their trainers and supervisors. Training courses at the CDP provide specific knowledge and expertise for deterrence, prevention and response to Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear and Explosive (CBRNE) incidents; mass casualty incidents; and incidents involving hazardous materials by providing advanced, hands-on and classroom-based state-of-the-art training. Armed Security Guard Services, as described in the attached draft SOW, includes but is not limited to providing properly qualified, trained, licensed, armed and certified personnel, their uniforms, equipment, tools, materials, supervision and other items and services except such equipment and supplies as provided by the Government necessary to: (1) plan for, and (2) provide continuous (24 hours per day, 7 days per week) static post and roving patrol armed security services to protect the CDP enclave; participation in site security surveys and inspections; provide operation and monitoring of the CDP security Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) and Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS); monitor fire alarm systems; participation in planning for and execution of CDP and Chemical, Ordnance, Biological, and Radiological Training Facility (COBRATF) Emergency Response Exercise (ERP) actions; performing visual inspection/security checks, via motorized and foot patrol of the CDP enclaves, and a full range of management duties including, but not limited to: planning, scheduling, and quality control. NAICS CODE is 561612 � Security Guards and Patrol Services. The Small Business Size Standard for this action is $29.0 million. PRODUCT SERVICE CODE (PSC): R430 Support- Professional: Physical Security and Badging The incumbent firm fixed priced contract for this requirement is 70FA2022C00000007 with IMAQ Walden JV LLC, 2700 GAMBELL ST, STE 401, ANCHORAGE AK 99503-2833 that was awarded as a competitive 8(a). ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE START DATE: August 2027 The Government desires that respondents offer their experience and recommendations on the following questions and issues related to the CDP requirements. The Government recommends that the respondent should first review the draft SOW so that the respondent may have a better insight on the questions below. (1) Is the SOW clear, concise, and/or sufficient enough to develop and submit the required information in response to a Request for Proposal (RFP)? (2) Discuss any other concerns, comments or recommendations you may have with the attached draft Statement of Work. (3) What is the business size standard of your company (small business, SDB, SDVOSB, HUBZone, Women-Owned, 8(a), Large, etc.)? If 8(a) eligible, please provide current status regarding your scheduled graduation date from the 8(a) program under this NAICS code(s). (4) Respondents to this RFI should describe their interest and ability to perform the requirements summarized within this notice, including examples of prior contract work of similar size, scope and complexity. (5) As part of the procurement process, a Pre-Proposal Site Visit is anticipated, but it may be a virtual pre-proposal site visit or it could be in person at CDP, Anniston, AL, approximately 10 days after the Solicitation/RFP has been issued. Further details regarding the Pre-Proposal Site Visit will be included in the FBO posting of the Final Solicitation/RFP. No inquiries will be answered at this time and respondents shall not be notified of the results of the market research. Again, this document is merely for market research and planning purposes only and does not constitute a commitment, implied, or otherwise, that a procurement action will be issued nor will the Government pay or reimburse for information solicited or produced and may not be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contract. In the event a solicitation is developed, it will be assigned a formal RFP number and the announcement will be published on www.sam.gov. Vendor comments may be incorporated and used to develop the final SOW as well as the solicitation. Responders to this RFI will not automatically be notified of any potential solicitation; therefore, interested parties should be vigilant in looking for and must respond to the official solicitation announcement when it is posted on GSA eBuy or www.sam.gov. Solicitation method will be decided upon based on results from this RFI and one posted on GSA eBuy. All responses to the RFI shall be submitted by email to Laura Harshbarger, C

title: Z2DA--FY27 EHRM | 657-21-702JC EHRM Training And Administrative Space Construction - St Louis John Cochran
description: INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting bids and subsequently awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract for the design-bid-build EHRM Training and Administrative Space Construction project at the St. Louis VA Health Care System (VAHCS) John Cochran campus located at 915 North Grand BLVD, St. Louis, MO 63106. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The VA Saint Louis Health Care System John Cochran Division requires a construction contractor to perform upgrades in support of the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) program. The construction area is located on the first floor of Building 2 and includes both training and administrative spaces. This project includes the execution of Phases 2, 3, and 4 of the associated design plans. Phase 2 addresses the North Training Rooms (Rooms 139, 140, 141, 142), totaling approximately 2,000 square feet. Work includes upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes. Phase 3 addresses the South Training Rooms (Rooms 126, 127, 128), totaling approximately 1,800 square feet. Work includes upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes. Additionally, Phase 3 includes the renovation of a 130-square-foot breakroom, with new floor and wall finishes, casework, a new sink, and a cold-water tie-in for an ice machine. Phase 4 addresses multiple areas: renovation of an approximately 1,400-square-foot corridor with new floor and wall finishes; upgrades to two offices (approximately 150 square feet each) with upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes; and upgrades to an existing data closet, including new floor and wall finishes, installation of an additional server rack with associated equipment, and replacement of the existing mini-split HVAC unit. Note: Phase 1 is excluded from this scope, as it was completed under a separate contract. Note: All power and data drops originally indicated as floor-mounted shall now be wall-mounted, as shown on revised drawings EP101 and TN101. Installation must match these updated sheet details; no floor-mounted outlets are permitted. ADMINISTRATIVE The solicitation will be issued as an Invitation for Bids (IFB) conducted in accordance with FAR part 14 and will be evaluated in accordance with the procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45.0 million. The solicitation will be issued in early to mid-October 2026. The period of performance is approximately 150 calendar days from the issuance of the notice to proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $250,000 and $500,000. This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to Amanda.Webster@va.gov. Telephone calls will not be accepted.

title: Yellow Ribbon Post-Deployment Event For 1-153 CAV
description: The objective of this Statement of Work is to conduct and complete the requirements for the 1-153 CAV Pre-Deployment Event with 330 total guests. It is the responsibility of the contractor to ensure all requested requirements are met. Event space, audio/visual (A/V) services, and catering services will be secured by the contractor with oversight from the Yellow Ribbon POC. Date: 9 January 2027 Hours: All convention space must be available for exclusive use from 0600-1500 on Saturday 09 January 2027. Lodging Hours: Hotel lodging must be available for exclusive use from 1700 on Friday 08 January 2027 until check out Sunday 10 January 2027. Location: Panama City Beach, FL The contractor shall provide a facility that will offer the following: parking lot, event space, audio/ visual equipment and technical support, catering and lodging. The contractor shall provide an on-site representative the day prior to the event, during the event, and after the completion of the event. This representative cannot be a member of the venue or hotel, it must come from the contracting agency. The Federal Government is tax exempt. CLIN 0001 - Catering Requirements: 1.0 A catered hot breakfast will be provided for approximately 330 adults. It will be served buffet style from 0700 to 0900 on 9 January 2027. Drink refreshments will remain available to guests until 1100. Buffet will include a hot meal with a minimum of two main entree choices, an assortment of breakfast pastries, and additional, common breakfast items (i.e. granola, yogurt, fruit, etc.). The buffet will also serve beverages including, but not limited to, hot coffee, juice(s), milk, water, and hot tea including sugar and cream. 1.1 Buffet will not serve 'fast food' items (i.e. french toast sticks, waffle tacos, Cinnamon Swirl Toast Breakfast Sandwiches, cheesy cheddar baco-biscuits, etc.). Egg dishes cannot be made from powdered eggs. Food menu items should avoid common allergies (i.e. shellfish) and clearly label allergens when necessary. At least one entree and one side dish must not include cheese. 1.2 The on-site representative is responsible for ensuring that catered food items conform to these requirements. Failure to meet these requirements will incur a claim from the government. 1.3 Catering services will provide flatware, plates, and condiments. With the exception of paper "to-go" coffee cups, plates and/or flatware must not be paper products. Catering services include set-up and clean-up. Flatware is encouraged to be made of a durable plastic that can be trashed after use. 1.4 Catering will be delivered to the event venue, ready to be served at 0700 9 January 2027. CLIN 0002 - Conference Space Requirements: 2.0 Room #1 � Large room for initial assembly to accommodate 330 guests, tables and chairs for seating, a stage, at least one trash can, and water stations. This room will likely need space to stage the catered breakfast and must provide tables so that guests can eat in this space. A scaled diagram of Room #1's set-up must be provided. See CLIN 0003 for Audio/Visual equipment requirements. 2.1 Registration/check-in area � If an in-house registration area is not available, three 6� tables with 6 chairs & two (2) trash cans shall be provided � Available 0600 - 1500, Saturday, 9 January 2027. 2.2 Room #2 - One room large enough to accommodate a capacity of 50 attendees with tables, chairs, and at least one water station. This room should be only a short distance (<2 minute walk) from room #1. This room will be used to host convention workshops and should include A/V equipment in accordance with CLIN 0003. 2.3 Room #3 - 40 6' vendor tables with two chairs at each table and at least one water station shall be provided in this room as the vendor area. The area should be big enough to host approximately 200 standing attendees and 40 6' vendor tables at any given time. This area may be co-located with room #1 or can be adjacent to room #1. Black table linens shall be provided for 10 tables. 2.4 Parking - Parking must be provided for attendees, vendors, and event staff (approximately 300 vehicles). Under no circumstances shall attendees, vendors, or event staff be required to pay for parking. CLIN 0003 - Audio/Visual Requirements: Audio/Visual and Technology Requirements: Cost shall be included in the total bill from the venue. Must NOT be a separate bill. 3.0 Room #1 A/V requirements: � 1 podium with microphone stand � 2 hand microphones with sound system � 1 screen with dimensions at least 6' by 6'. This may be a projector screen. � 1 A/V cart or projector (if needed) � A stage 3.1 Room #2 A/V requirements: � 2 hand microphones with sound system � 1 screen with dimensions at least 6' by 6'. This may be a projector screen. � 1 A/V cart or projector (if needed) A technician must be on site for trouble shooting the day before and the day of event. CLIN 0004 - Lodging Requirements: 4.0 The Federal Government is tax exempt. Vendor accommodations must be within 10 miles of the event venue. Multiple lodging venues may be used to meet this requirement. All lodging venues to be used are subject to the requirements specified in CLIN 0004. The on-site representative must be able to meet Yellow Ribbon staff at the lodging venue(s), if requested. The on-site representative is responsible for ensuring that event-attendees identified by the Yellow Ribbon Coordinator who qualify to receive lodging are able to successfully check-in to the lodging venue without complications. 4.1 Attendees who meet our requirements for lodging will start to arrive the day prior to the event. The amount of rooms required are: � 45 rooms for the night of Friday, 8 January 2027 � 15 rooms for the night of Saturday, 9 January 2027 4.2 Lodging facilities shall meet the American with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements and provide ADA compliant rooms. A preliminary requirement for ADA compliant sleep rooms and special room requirements will be provided by 18 December 2026. 4.3 All rooms provided under this contract shall be non-smoking rooms. The venue will not be undergoing renovations during event dates. Overnight and daily parking will be included in the contract for 45 vehicles on the days/nights of 8-9 January 2027. The parking area must be within walking distance of the lodging venue and not require a shuttle service to the front lobby of the venue. 4.4 Personal Expenses: Personal expenses in guest rooms such as long distance phone charges, movie rentals, laundry, room service, etc. will be paid by the guest and shall not be billed under the resultant contract. NOTE: If cash or credit card is not available, incidental services shall be blocked for use in the room. The lodging venue may not deny qualified or identified event attendees the use of lodging if the attendee does not present a credit card for incidentals. 4.5 The Yellow Ribbon Coordinator may review the offered hotel facilities prior to awarding a contract at his or her discretion. The contractor shall provide facilities that will offer the following: lighted parking lot, an exercise room, functional elevators, and ice machines. The Contractor shall provide an on-site representative to mediate complications and concerns while event attendees check-in and check-out from their rooms and all times between. The on-site representative must be a representative from the contracting agency and cannot be a member of the hotel staff. 4.6 The lodging venue(s) should include a gym/fitness center, 24-hour front desk assistance, business services, a pool, and laundry services. Rooms should be spacious and include showers with warm water, a working refrigerator, free wi-fi, air conditioning and heating, a flat-screen television, furnishings complete with a desk, closet, chair(s), and an alarm clock. Hotel facilities must be free of pests (e.g. cockroaches). 4.7 Most importantly, the venue must be located in a low-crime area where attendees feel safe walking alone at night. The Yellow Ribbon C
