title: Install Generator- FCI Bastrop
description: Solicitation The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) is issuing solicitation 15BBNF27Q50100001 for the award of a firm-fixed-price construction contract for a project entitled Install Generator at the Federal Correctional Institution (FCI Bastrop), located in Bastrop, TX. FCI Bastrop is a federal correctional facility located at 1341 Highway 95 North, Bastrop, TX, 78602. The project consists of the following: replace the existing 750 KW Generator, load bank, and 3-way Main Switchgear and install one (1) new 2000 KW Diesel Generator and Switchgear system. See the Statement of Work/Specifications attachment included with the solicitation posting for the complete requirements of the work. The performance period for the project will be 420 Calendar Days from issuance of the notice to proceed. The NAICS code for this requirement is 238210 with a corresponding small business size standard of $19 million. The solicitation will be distributed solely through the Contract Opportunity website at https://www.sam.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be made available. The website provides download instructions. The "Sensitive /Secure package Upload" option will be selected for this procurement. All secure/locked documents uploaded, to include the solicitation, will require an active SAM vendor registration to obtain access. In addition, only those vendors who have been issued a valid Marketing Partner Identification Number (MPIN) from www.sam.gov will be granted access. If your firm does not have the NAICS code listed in www.sam.gov required for this solicitation, an email may be forwarded to your firm requesting an explanation as to why your firm should be granted access. If you encounter problems accessing these documents, please contact the Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220. All future information about this solicitation, including any amendments, will also be distributed solely through this website. Interested parties are responsible for continuously monitoring this website to ensure that they have the most recent information about this proposed contract action. IMPORTANT: Any contractor interested in obtaining a contract award with the Federal Bureau of Prisons must be registered in https://www.sam.gov. In order to qualify for award, your business size metrics information entered in your www.sam.gov SAM registration must be less than or equal to the size standard specified above. Each bidder's www.sam.gov registration will be reviewed by the Government to confirm that your business size meets the small business size standard requirement. All bidders are urged to double check their www.sam.gov registration and update as necessary, including the size metrics information. This is a 100 percent small business set-aside. You must be registered in www.sam.gov as a small business for the applicable NAICS code (see FAR provision 52.219-1 in the Representations & Certifications section of your www.sam.gov registration).

title: FCI MCKEAN FY27 2ND QTR BREAD
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution (FCI) McKean, Bradford, Pennsylvania, herein issues solicitation 15B20927Q00000005 for the requirements of: BREAD ITEMS 2ND QUARTER FY 2027. This solicitation is UNRESTICTED. FOB Destination, delivery dates will begin JANUARY 4TH, 2027 and continue throughout the period of performance ending MARCH 31ST, 2027. By bidding on these items, you are confirming that you can make delivery within this time frame. BIWEEKLY deliveries will be required dependent on the current inmate population. Any delivery that is not within this timeframe can be refused, in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulations. Deliveries will be made to the FCI McKean Warehouse, 6975 Route 59, Lewis Run, PA 16738, 15 Miles South of Bradford, PA. The bread is to be delivered on plastic racks to avoid destruction of goods. The contract type is a firm-fixed price. The Government reserves the right upon award to make formal single or multiple awards. The Government will award to the responsible offerors whose bid, conforming to the solicitation, is most advantageous to the Government, with both past performance and price considered. The solicitation will be available on NOVEMBER 18, 2026 at 8:00 AM EST and will be posted to the General Services Administration Federal Business Opportunities website: www.sam.gov. All future information about this acquisition, including solicitation amendments, will be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure they have the most up-to-date information about this solicitation. All contractors doing business with the Federal Government shall be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database. The website for registration is: www.sam.gov. The closing date for receipt of quotes is DECEMBER 2ND, 2026 at 2:00 PM EST. Payment will be made using Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) through a purchase order or utilizing a purchase card. Faith-based and community-based organizations have the right to submit offers/quotes equally with other organizations for contracts for which they are eligible. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 311812. Vendors who submit an offer concur that the delivery date can be met, unless otherwise specified (example, biweekly bread deliveries). Substitutions to specifications in line-item descriptions are prohibited, (example, size and case count.) We reserve the right to request a sample of product prior to award for perishable items. The point of contact for all information regarding this solicitation is Alyssa McGrew, Contract Specialist, at the address listed below and telephone number (814) 362-8900, extension 3422 and/or Cory Sudbrook at (814)362 8900 extension 3419. Completed offers must be emailed to amcgrew@bop.gov and csudbrook@bop.gov or faxed to (814) 363-6815. Emails are preferred. If you do not receive a confirmation email, please call to verify. The anticipated award date is DECEMBER 7, 2026.

title: Commercial Gear Backup Power (CGBP) and Control System Improvements at Fish Barrier
description: I. PURPOSE AND DISCLAIMER**********************The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Chicago District, is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement for upgrading our Commercial Gear Backup Power (CGBP) and associated control system at our electronic fish barrier located in Romeoville, Illinois. We are seeking to identify qualified Small Business concerns (including 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB, and Small Business Joint Ventures/Teaming Arrangements) and Other-Than-Small Business concerns capable of performing this requirement. The intention is to procure these services on a competitive basis.**********************BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES (IN FULL OR IN PART) OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION, and multiple awards MAY be made. All Small Business Set-Aside categories will be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions.**********************DISCLAIMER**********************THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ANY ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this Sources Sought.********************************************II. COMPREHENSIVE TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION and PROJECT SCOPE********************************************The Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier facility requires a complex industrial electrical power generation, backup power, and automation and control system modernization project. This system is a critical component of the federal effort to prevent the movement of invasive aquatic species between the Great Lakes and Mississippi River basins. **********************Specifically, USACE needs to upgrade the backup generator and switchgear control systems at Permanent Barrier 1 (PB1) to correct unreliable operation caused by deficiencies in the original design, configuration, and wiring. The project requires replacing generator controllers, modernizing breaker controls and communications, and rebuilding the control software and operator interfaces to improve reliable operation on utility and backup power. Work will require testing, operator training, and a phased changeover to maintain continuous barrier operations. Work will be performed at an active, mission-critical facility requiring careful coordination with ongoing operations, planned equipment outages, and system changeovers to maintain operational readiness and minimize disruptions. A critical requirement is the integration of new equipment into an active industrial facility while protecting existing operations. The anticipated work may include engineering, design review, equipment upgrades and replacement, control system programming, integration, testing, and commissioning of interconnected electrical and industrial automation systems. ******************************************************************TECHNICAL CAPABILITIES:******************************************************************The project requires specialized expertise in: a) generator synchronization and load management, b) switchgear automation, c) protective relaying, d) programmable logic controllers (PLCs), e) human-machine interfaces (HMIs), industrial communications, and associated monitoring and data management systems.**********************Contractors must possess the technical capabilities necessary to work with the existing systems and integrate new equipment while maintaining compatibility and functionality. The existing facility incorporates Rockwell Automation ControlLogix PLCs, FactoryTalk View SE, FactoryTalk Transaction Manager, Microsoft SQL Server, Basler generator synchronization and control equipment, Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL) protective relays and RTAC equipment, and DEIF generator controllers. ATTACHMENT NOTICE: Interested parties must carefully review Attachment 1 (Equipment_SOW.xlsx ??? PB1 Equipment Modernization and SOW Matrix) attached to this notice in PIEE, the DoW Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment, which details the specific equipment removals, modifications, additions, hard-wired control conversions, I/O transitions, and as-built drawing updates (across four separate contractor drawing sets) required under our anticipated scope.**********************Contractors must demonstrate their capability of obtaining a specialized Master Systems Integrator (MSI) or Industrial Automation and Control Systems (IACS) engineering firm to perform any needed engineering, programming, integration, testing, commissioning, and troubleshooting of the complex interconnected industrial control systems.**********************Contractors must demonstrate their ability to obtain qualified personnel. Qualified personnel include Electrical Generating Systems Association (EGSA) certified technicians or personnel possessing equivalent documented qualifications to support generator-related engineering, design reviews, integration, testing, and commissioning. If proposing to use equivalent, provide what documentation your firm considers as equivalent for USACE consideration.**********************The contractor must possess the technical and organizational capabilities to execute phased modifications, coordinate authorized shutdowns and system changeovers, implement temporary control arrangements where necessary, perform pre-commissioning and acceptance testing, and develop contingency measures to minimize operational disruptions and maintain the safety, reliability, and continuity of existing barrier operations.**********************III. REQUESTED INFORMATION FROM INTERESTED PARTIES********************************************Interested firms are invited to submit a Capability Statement (not to exceed 10 pages) addressing the following four (4) sections after reviewing the technical capability narrative above and Attachment 1 (Equipment_SOW.xlsx):SECTION A: ADMINISTRATIVE AND BUSINESS SIZE********************************************1. Company Name, Address, Point of Contact, telephone number and email, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI).**********************2. Business Size under NAICS 238210 ($19.0M Size Standard) and all applicable socioeconomic designations.**********************3. If proposing as a Small Business, confirm your understanding of FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting) and your ability to perform at least 25% of the cost of contract performance (excluding the cost of materials) with your own organization or similarly situated small business entities. **********************4. Should this requirement be solicited as Full and Open Competition, other-than-small-business offerors will be required to submit an acceptable Small Business Subcontracting Plan in accordance with RFO 19.1

title: Small Arms Fire Control - Basic Capability Industry Day
description: SPECIAL NOTICE Call for Participants � Product Manager Soldier Weapons Small Arms Fire Control � Basic Capability Industry Day *Updated 19 NOV 2026 - Changes identified with an asterisk. Notice ID: TBD Document Type: Special Notice Response Date: 02 December 2026 NLT 1400EST Classification Code: TBD PSC: 1240 � Optical Sighting and Ranging Equipment NAICS: 332994 � Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing This notice serves as a notification for the event. All dates presented in this notice are estimates and are subject to change. Small Arms Fire Control � Basic Capability (SAFC � BC): The USG will host a SAFC � BC Industry Day on 08 December 2026 from 0800-1600 EST, to provide Program Overview, review draft acquisition strategy, and share USG information. A No-Host Social will follow the event. The SAFC � BC Industry Day will be held at Hilton Garden Inn � Rockaway (375 Mount Hope Ave., Rockaway NJ 07866 (973-328-0600)). Group rate available in limited quantity. The SAFC - BC system is envisioned as commercial/non-developmental weapon-mounted standalone reflexive/holographic sight with magnifier, as well as an aiming laser. The system will combine the close range, rapid target engagement capabilities of the M68 Close Combat Optic (CCO), the magnified capabilities of the M150 Rifle Combat Optic (RCO) and the aiming laser capabilities of a PEQ-15 - all while being able to withstand mechanical stress profiles created by weapon recoil and conform to MIL-STD-810 environmental conditions. Attendance at the Industry Day is limited and requires Government approval. All visitors will be required to fill in and submit the required form(s) identified below on or before 02 December 2026. For security purposes there will be no walk-ins or unregistered visitors allowed. There will be no one-on-one sessions the day of the event, but there will be opportunity for interested parties to sign up for a session. Detailed information will be in the Welcome Packet which will be provided upon RSVP. All participating companies will be required to provide the two following documents: 1. A Non-disclosure Agreement (NDA); and 2. an Attendee List including name and email prior to attending the event. By signing the NDA, attendees agree to use such information only for purposes authorized in connection with the meeting and not to disclose it to any third party without prior written authorization. See Attachment section of this Special Notice for blank NDA Form and use the following fill-ins: Contract No.: N/A Solicitation No.: PANDTA-27-P-0000 041362 *IMPORTANT: A signed/approved DD2345 is required for attendance. A blank DD2345 is attached and detailed instructions, in addition to those in the form, can be found at DLA.mil. description: This Sources Sought Notice is issued as a means of conducting market research to identify any/all parties, to include large and small businesses, having an interest in and the resources to support the requirements for Registration, Storage and Distribution of Chemicals and Drugs for Pre-Clinical Discovery Evaluation and Development. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. Interested parties are expected to review this notice and the draft Statement of Work (SOW) to familiarize themselves with the requirement of this project; failure to do so will be at your firm�s own risk. The Drug Synthesis and Chemistry Branch (DSCB) of the Developmental Therapeutics Program (DTP) of the Division of Cancer Treatment and Diagnosis (DCTD) of the National Cancer Institute (NCI) is seeking support services to operate and maintain the National Cancer Institute�s Chemotherapeutic Agents Repository (NCI-CAR). This acquisition is responsible for providing an informational interface with NCI and external investigators that are submitting or requesting research compounds; for updating of the chemical database which includes chemical, inventory, receiving and shipping information; systematic file and record keeping of both current and archival information related to repository activities; and reacquisition of samples for continued chemical and biological studies. Towards this goal, the Program acquires and evaluates about 5,000 single agents each year in anticancer assays. In addition, research samples are provided to the general research community both in vialed and plated format. NCI-CAR is responsible for receiving, storage and distribution services along with curating an inventory of approximately 500,000 - 600,000 individual samples and associated chemical, inventory and distribution data. Approximately 400 samples are received monthly, registered and shipped to NCI testing facilities; an additional 2,500 samples are weighed monthly from inventory and shipped to research investigators both in the U.S. (including NCI) and foreign countries. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to identify all potentially capable, interested sources. title: Maintenance Dredging of New York and New Jersey Harbor � Arthur Kill 50 foot Reach Federal Navigation Project
description: Market Survey Background Information The New York District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) proposes to perform maintenance dredging of the New York and New Jersey Harbor � Arthur Kill 50 foot Reach Federal Navigation Project to a depth of -50 feet Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) plus 1 foot of allowable over-depth. The proposed maintenance dredging would remove approximately 150,000 cubic yards (CY) of material from the critical shoal area. The dredged material would be dredged and subsequently placed at a suitable, contractor provided, state permitted upland placement site(s). The dredged material is expected to consist primarily of silt, clay, and some sand. Based on the past dredging projects within the New York Harbor, and anticipated restrictions found in the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation Water Quality Certificate, the proposed work can only be performed by utilizing a mechanical clamshell dredge with environmental bucket. Additionally, tug-boats, sealed hull barges and survey vessels will be needed to perform the work during the dredging, transport, processing and placement activities. The dredging, transport and placement at a suitable, contractor provided, state permitted upland placement site(s) would be required to meet all federal, state, and local criteria required by the government agencies having jurisdiction where the dredging and placement sites are located. All necessary permits required for the dredged material placement will be provided by the contractor to the government. The apparent low bidder shall, within 35 calendar days from the date the apparent low bidder is notified of being such, provide copies of all required permits and approvals for transportation, transfer, dewatering, processing, and final placement of dredged material, and shall submit evidence of such permits and approvals to the government. Once the contract is awarded, the contractor will be required to commence work within five (5) calendar days after the date of receipt of the Notice to Proceed and maintain an integrated production rate of at least 3,000 cubic yards per calendar day for the dredging and placement of the dredged material. The presence of the dredging equipment in the channel will impact ship traffic, and it is necessary to maintain this production rate while minimizing the duration of this impact. The proposed work is anticipated to take place in the summer / fall of 2027. SURVEY OF THE DREDGING INDUSTRY The following confidential survey questionnaire is designed to apprise USACE of prospective dredging contractors� project execution capabilities. Please provide your response to the following questions. All questions are in regard to the Arthur Kill 50 foot Reach maintenance dredging project. General 1. Have you ever worked on dredging jobs similar in nature to this project? If so, please describe the project and for whom the work was performed. Identify a point of contact and phone number, as a reference of relevant experience. 2. Have you performed dredging within the waters of the Port of New York and New Jersey? 3. Do you have experience with the placement of dredged material at a suitable, contractor provided, state permitted upland placement site? Please list your experience. 4. What percentage of work (volume of material dredged, transported, processed and ultimately placed) can you perform with your own equipment or equipment owned by another dredging contractor? 5. Would you be willing to bid on the project previously described? If the answer is No, please explain why not. 6. Would you be bidding on this project as a sole contractor, prime contractor with subcontractor(s) or as a joint venture? 7. Is there a dollar limit on the size of contract that you would bid? If so, what is that limit? 8. What is the largest dredging contract, in dollars, on which you were the prime contractor? 9. What is your bonding capacity per contract? What is your total bonding capacity? 10. Do you have experience using USACE Resident Management System (RMS) 3.0 for delivering Submittals, Daily Dredging Reports and Pay Estimates? 11. In the event that the USACE transitions from Resident Management System (RMS) to an alternative construction management system during the contract, will the contractor be ready to adapt to the new management system? 12. Do you have experience applying USACE EM 385-1-1 (Mar 2024) and all requirements? Deficiencies observed on site will require immediate attention and action to meet all applicable safety codes. Equipment 13. What type of dredge equipment do you own and/or operate that is suitable for the work described? Do you own a mechanical dredge with a closed environmental clamshell bucket? Please list each piece of equipment capable of performing the work described, i.e. dredging, transfer, transportation, processing and final placement of the material. For each dredge that you list, please specify its bucket size(s), and any other salient characteristics. 14. Identify which dredge(s), including support equipment (tug, crew boat, scows, etc.), you would employ on this project. Also, for each dredge, identify the maximum dredging depth. 15. Do you own material scows? If so, how many do you have available for use? Please list the name of the scow, its type (ocean-going, sealed hull, etc) and the capacity. 16. Do you have the capability to process the dredged material on your own? If so please explain. If not, what commercial provider of dredge material processing will you engage for this project? What is the daily processing capacity in either case? 17. Will you be able to meet a production rate of 3,000 cubic yards per calendar day and complete all work? 18. Do you have experience with the use of an automated Dredged Material Monitoring System (Black Box / Silent Inspector) employing a Dredged Material Inspector (DMI)?

title: Small Arms Fire Control - Basic Capability Industry Day
description: SPECIAL NOTICE Call for Participants � Product Manager Soldier Weapons Small Arms Fire Control � Basic Capability Industry Day *Updated 19 NOV 2026 - Changes identified with an asterisk. Notice ID: TBD Document Type: Special Notice Response Date: 02 December 2026 NLT 1400EST Classification Code: TBD PSC: 1240 � Optical Sighting and Ranging Equipment NAICS: 332994 � Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing This notice serves as a notification for the event. All dates presented in this notice are estimates and are subject to change. Small Arms Fire Control � Basic Capability (SAFC � BC): The USG will host a SAFC � BC Industry Day on 08 December 2026 from 0800-1600 EST, to provide Program Overview, review draft acquisition strategy, and share USG information. A No-Host Social will follow the event. The SAFC � BC Industry Day will be held at Hilton Garden Inn � Rockaway (375 Mount Hope Ave., Rockaway NJ 07866 (973-328-0600)). Group rate available in limited quantity. The SAFC - BC system is envisioned as commercial/non-developmental weapon-mounted standalone reflexive/holographic sight with magnifier, as well as an aiming laser. The system will combine the close range, rapid target engagement capabilities of the M68 Close Combat Optic (CCO), the magnified capabilities of the M150 Rifle Combat Optic (RCO) and the aiming laser capabilities of a PEQ-15 - all while being able to withstand mechanical stress profiles created by weapon recoil and conform to MIL-STD-810 environmental conditions. Attendance at the Industry Day is limited and requires Government approval. All visitors will be required to fill in and submit the required form(s) identified below on or before 02 December 2026. For security purposes there will be no walk-ins or unregistered visitors allowed. There will be no one-on-one sessions the day of the event, but there will be opportunity for interested parties to sign up for a session. Detailed information will be in the Welcome Packet which will be provided upon RSVP. All participating companies will be required to provide the two following documents: 1. A Non-disclosure Agreement (NDA); and 2. an Attendee List including name and email prior to attending the event. By signing the NDA, attendees agree to use such information only for purposes authorized in connection with the meeting and not to disclose it to any third party without prior written authorization. See Attachment section of this Special Notice for blank NDA Form and use the following fill-ins: Contract No.: N/A Solicitation No.: PANDTA-27-P-0000 041362 *IMPORTANT: A signed/approved DD2345 is required for attendance. Instructions can be found at DLA.mil. For foreign companies, non-US citizens, and/or US citizens representing foreign companies, please provide your name, country of citizenship, and company to the POC below and further registration directions will be provided. Notes: (a) The USG does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this Special Notice or to otherwise pay for the information solicited except as an allowable cost under other contracts as provided in subsection 31.205-18, bid and proposal costs, of the Federal Acquisition Regulation. (b) Although "proposal", "offeror", �respondent�, �contractor� or �industry� may be used in this Special Notice, your response will be treated as information only. It shall not be used as a proposal. (c) This Special Notice is issued for the purpose of informing Industry regarding future contracting plans and soliciting feedback. (d) No award is intended as a result of this Special Notice nor does the USG intend to pay for information received. Any response to this notice is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the USG to form a binding contract. (e) There are no vendor costs to participate in this event. A lack of participation in the SAFC - BC Industry Day does not preclude participation in any future solicitations, if any are issued. (f) The USG will not be responsible for any expenses incurred by a vendor�s decision to participate in the SAFC - BC Industry Day. title: Request for Information: U.S. Shipyard and Vessel Construction Manager Capability for Floating Drydock Construction
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is conducting market research to identify qualified U.S.-based shipyards and Vessel Construction Managers (VCMs) capable of supporting the detailed production design, construction, testing, and delivery of a new 8,000 long-ton capacity floating drydock (FDD) before calendar year 2030. The Government anticipates awarding a Firm-Fixed-Price contract through a prime VCM, who will partner with a qualified domestic shipyard to execute the build under American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) survey and classification based on a Government-furnished contract design. Interested parties are encouraged to review the attached Request for Information (RFI) and submit responses in accordance with the instructions provided.

title: Install Generator- FCI Bastrop
description: Amendment 0001- Correct Set Aside error in the Instruction to Offerors Solicitation The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) is issuing solicitation 15BBNF27Q50100001 for the award of a firm-fixed-price construction contract for a project entitled Install Generator at the Federal Correctional Institution (FCI Bastrop), located in Bastrop, TX. FCI Bastrop is a federal correctional facility located at 1341 Highway 95 North, Bastrop, TX, 78602. The project consists of the following: replace the existing 750 KW Generator, load bank, and 3-way Main Switchgear and install one (1) new 2000 KW Diesel Generator and Switchgear system. See the Statement of Work/Specifications attachment included with the solicitation posting for the complete requirements of the work. The performance period for the project will be 420 Calendar Days from issuance of the notice to proceed. The NAICS code for this requirement is 238210 with a corresponding small business size standard of $19 million. The solicitation will be distributed solely through the Contract Opportunity website at https://www.sam.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be made available. The website provides download instructions. The "Sensitive /Secure package Upload" option will be selected for this procurement. All secure/locked documents uploaded, to include the solicitation, will require an active SAM vendor registration to obtain access. In addition, only those vendors who have been issued a valid Marketing Partner Identification Number (MPIN) from www.sam.gov will be granted access. If your firm does not have the NAICS code listed in www.sam.gov required for this solicitation, an email may be forwarded to your firm requesting an explanation as to why your firm should be granted access. If you encounter problems accessing these documents, please contact the Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220. All future information about this solicitation, including any amendments, will also be distributed solely through this website. Interested parties are responsible for continuously monitoring this website to ensure that they have the most recent information about this proposed contract action. IMPORTANT: Any contractor interested in obtaining a contract award with the Federal Bureau of Prisons must be registered in https://www.sam.gov. In order to qualify for award, your business size metrics information entered in your www.sam.gov SAM registration must be less than or equal to the size standard specified above. Each bidder's www.sam.gov registration will be reviewed by the Government to confirm that your business size meets the small business size standard requirement. All bidders are urged to double check their www.sam.gov registration and update as necessary, including the size metrics information. This is a 100 percent small business set-aside. You must be registered in www.sam.gov as a small business for the applicable NAICS code (see FAR provision 52.219-1 in the Representations & Certifications section of your www.sam.gov registration).

title: Biomedical Research Application Evaluation and Support (BRAES)
description: This is a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Biomedical Research Application Evaluation and Support (BRAES) on behalf of the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) within the Defense Health Agency (DHA) located in Frederick, MD at Fort Detrick. This requirement is a performance-based non-commercial, non-personal services support requirement and will be awarded as a Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quality (MA-IDIQ) contract. The CDMRP requires BRAES is for: 1) Funding opportunity announcement set-up within CDMRP electronic Biomedical Research Application Portal (eBRAP) (eBRAP task order awarded to a single vendor); 2) Oversight of electronic receipt and processing of intramural and extramural pre- and full research applications in eBRAP (eBRAP task order awarded to a single vendor); 3) Application compliance review in eBRAP (eBRAP task order awarded to a single vendor); and 4) Scientific merit peer review including operation of a secure Contractor-owned, Contractor-operated web-based electronic system which supports all activities and capabilities specific to peer review (i.e. Scientific Administration and Management/SAM) (SAM task orders awarded to multiple vendors). NOTE: The task orders associated with scientific peer review will be competed as fair opportunity between the successful BRAES Contract holders AFTER award of this MA IDIQ.

description: Amendment 3 (11/09/2026): ISO updates to Part II - Technical Areas & Requirements: TA1: Edits to the "Target" language for the Retrospective Data Access metric. Provides Attachment A2 for TA1 Solution Summary Requirements and Attachment A3 for TA2 Solution Summary Requirements. Amendment 1 (10/14/2026): Update due dates and/or times of all TAs SPECTRA will identify and act on autism trajectories, the evolving developmental paths individuals follow across the lifespan from the prenatal period through aging, spanning autism characteristics, co-occurring conditions, and functional outcomes together with the genetic, biological, behavioral, iatrogenic (medical influences), environmental factors and their nonlinear interactions. Rather than examining these factors in isolation, SPECTRA will examine how they combine and interact, including their nonlinear interactions, to produce autism and its co-occurring conditions over time. SPECTRA will also develop technologies that serve two purposes at once: extending reliable assessment beyond the clinic while improving everyday communication, function, and quality of life. The same tools people use to live more fully will also generate the data that drive measurement and personalized care.

title: ND OMAD 2025(1) Minuteman Missile Access Road
description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Office of Missile Air Defense Program (OMAD) is a Defense Access Road (DAR) program used by the Department of Defense (DoD) to fund the annual maintenance and improvements on certified gravel roads. FHWA works with the Military Surface Deployment and Distribution Command (SDDC) to support the Air Force Intercontinental Ballistic Missile Program (Minuteman). These Minuteman Missile Access Roads are located in 6 counties within North Dakota. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The work includes roadway reconditioning and adding four inches of aggregate surface course as well as the replacement of culverts. All proposed work is to stay on the existing roadway bench. The proposed typical section consists of reconditioning the existing gravel roadway per Section 303 and adding an additional 4-inches of Aggregate Surface Course with a maximum width of 24-feet. A 4% crown is proposed or as approved by the CO. The Contractor will need to taper down the proposed aggregate surface, per the typical section, at applicable locations.

title: Field of Testing
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) in Fort Detrick, MD intends to negotiate on a sole source basis (IAW RFO 12.102(a)) with American Industrial Hygiene Association (AIHA), 3120 Fairview Park Dr Suite 360, Falls Church, VA 22042, as the only responsible source that can provide AIHA Lab Accreditation. This is a pre-solicitation notice in accordance with RFO 5.101. The laboratory is required to participate in the AIHA PAT Programs in every Field of Testing (FoT) accredited by AIHA LAP, LLC. The contractor shall provide the appropriate Proficiency Analytical Testing (PAT) rounds to meet minimum requirements per AIHA LAP, LLC accreditation in order to be compliant in every Field of Testing (FoT). AIHA LAP, LLC is the only entity that can provide services that will meet the requirement of Proficiency Analytical Testing (PAT) Program participation. This cquisition is being conducted under simplified acquisition procedures. There are no set-aside restrictions for this requirement. The intended procurement will be classified under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 334516 with a Small Business Size Standard of 500 or fewer employees. This pre-solicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation document exists for this requirement. However, any parties interested in responding to this notice shall submit technical data, including cost, sufficient to determine capability in providing the same service. All capability statements received by closing of this notification of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement. Based on the above information, the only technically acceptable subscription can be provided by AIHA. Submit email capability statements (using PDF, MS Word, Excel attachments) to Brian Miller at brian.d.miller1.civ@health.mil. Statements are due no later than 3:00 PM ET, 2 December 2026. No phone calls will be accepted.

title: Announcement for Partnership Proposals: Atmospheric Exploration Observatory
description: NASA�s Science Mission Directorate (SMD), Earth Science Division (ESD), is inviting innovative partnership proposals for the Atmospheric Exploration Observatory to explore collaborative opportunities for hardware utilization. title: Announcement for Partnership Proposals: Atmospheric Exploration Observatory
description: NASA�s Science Mission Directorate (SMD), Earth Science Division (ESD), is inviting innovative partnership proposals for the Atmospheric Exploration Observatory to explore collaborative opportunities for hardware utilization. NASA is exploring partnerships with external organizations to enable more impactful exploitation of NASA resources and to advance the commercial remote sensing industry. This Announcement for Partnership Proposals (AFPP) invites proposals for innovative partnerships for atmospheric exploration. This AFPP envisions one or more partnerships to complete the former GeoCarb instrument, integrate the instrument with a spacecraft, launch, operate, and share its unique data with clear benefits to the selected partner(s). On or after the publication date of this SAM.gov special notice, the full, final text for this AFPP will be available for download from the NASA Solicitation and Proposal Integrated Review and Evaluation System (NSPIRES) at https://nspires.nasaprs.com by searching on the SAM notice ID (called a solicitation number on NSPIRES) or via the link provided below. NASA may periodically update the submission website, including announcing meetings with log-on details for interested parties. It is the responsibility of interested parties and the proposer to stay up to date with that website and ensure that they have the latest information available. All meetings and forums will be virtual.

title: CO OMAD 300(71) Minuteman Missile Access
description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Office of Missile Air Defense Program (OMAD) is a Defense Access Road (DAR) program used by the Department of Defense (DoD) to fund the annual maintenance and improvements on certified gravel roads. FHWA works with the Military Surface Deployment and Distribution Command (SDDC) to support the Air Force Intercontinental Ballistic Missile Program (Minuteman). These Minuteman Missile Access Roads are located in southwestern Wyoming, southeastern Nebraska, and northeastern Colorado. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The work includes roadway reconditioning and adding four inches of aggregate surface course as well as the replacement of culverts. All proposed work is to stay on the existing roadway bench. The proposed typical section consists of reconditioning the existing gravel roadway per Section 303 and adding an additional 4-inches of Aggregate Surface Course with a maximum width of 24-feet. A 4% crown is proposed or as approved by the CO. The Contractor will need to taper down the proposed aggregate surface, per the typical section, at applicable locations.

title: Local & Long-Distance Telecommunications Service-Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska
description: 673 CS seeks telecommunications services where the contractor is required to provide, troubleshoot, and maintain comprehensive, continuous (24/7/365+) telecommunication services for Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), AK ensuring operational reliability of 99.999%. This scope encompasses local, domestic long-distance, international long-distance, and toll-free telecommunication services (LLTS). The contractor must supply all necessary transmission facilities, equipment, and maintenance up to the demarcation points, operating in full compliance with Federal Communications Commission (FCC), Programmable Unified Communications (PUC), Department of War (DoW), and Air Force standards.

title: Flooring Requirement Contract Solicitation
description: The 319th Contracting Squadron, Grand Forks AFB, North Dakota, is issuing this Solicitation as a means to Request for Quotes (RFQ) to identify parties to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Requirements Contract for the following: The work under this project consists of providing all material, equipment, and labor necessary for maintaining flooring/carpeting and other services necessary to perform Grand Forks Air Force Flooring work for GFAFB in accordance with the attached specifications. The work may include, but is not limited to, the following: Verification of Dimensions, Flooring Removal, Patch flooring, Surface Preparation, Installation, Disposal of Debris, and Furnishing Flooring as described in the attached documents. Quotes are due by 2 December 2026 at 3:00PM CST and shall be submitted electronically to SSgt Asante Nieves, Contract Specialist at asante.nieves@us.af.mil or Ms. Monique Padilla, Contracting Officer at monique.padilla.3@us.af.mil. Quoters must review all solicitation attachments for complete performance requirements. If proposal file size exceeds email limits, the offeror must request a DoD SAFE link from the POCs in advance of the due date. The current applicable wage determination is included and any updates prior to award or task order issuance will apply. All solicitation updates will be posted to SAM.gov.

title: THRUST ACTUATOR
description: The contractor shall furnish all services, facilities, labor, parts, materials, equipment, tools, and data necessary to accomplish the inspection and overhaul for the following assets: Noun: Thrust Actuator NSN: 1680-01-496-7234 P/N: 145H7300-26 Estimated Quantity: 5 Each Minimum - 90 Each Maximum The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 336413 and the size standard is 1,250 employees. The proposed contractual action will be a Five (5) year, Firm Fixed Price, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), maintenance and overhaul contract, with minimum/maximum quantities listed above. Although DMWR 1-1650-397 is adequate for overhaul of the Thrust Actuator, overhaul is restricted to approved sources only. This is a Critical Safety Item (CSI) and must be overhauled by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) or other approved sources. The technical data pertinent to this requirement is owned exclusively by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), The Boeing Company and the other approved source is AAR Allen Services, Inc. The Boeing Company and AAR Allen Services, Inc. have exclusive rights to the technical data package and are the only two approved sources. Interested parties must have secured the rights to the technical data package to be a potential source for the overhaul of this part. If a new source acquires the proprietary data from the approved sources during the contract period of performance, the new source can compete in future procurements. The Servocylinder is identified as a CSI. This procurement is restricted to The Boeing Company (CAGE 77272) and AAR Allen Services, Inc. (CAGE Code 26101). An RFP will be issued at a later date for this requirement. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement and any follow-up information requested. No basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to this announcement or Government use of any information provided. All responsible sources may submit an offer which shall be considered by the agency. The closing date annotated is an estimated date dependent upon the date of the release of the solicitation; however; the solicitation will not open prior to the closing date stated on the synopsis. No telephone requests for the solicitation will be accepted. Point of Contact: Arthur Gunter, email: arthur.l.gunter.civ@army.mil. Foreign firms are reminded that all requests for solicitation must be processed through their respective embassies. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the Agency. This requirement is currently unfunded. Award will be withheld pending receipt of sufficient funds.

title: Kauniaisten keskusta-alueen vision laatiminen
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Kauniaisten keskusta-alueen vision laatiminen tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteenä olevan alustavantyöohjelman mukaisesti. Hankinta sisältää keskusta-alueen vision laatimisen, tarvittavan suunnittelu- ja asiantuntijatyön, vuorovaikutuksen suunnittelun ja toteuttamisen sekä alustavassa työohjelmassa määriteltyjen aineistojen tuottamisen. Työn tavoitteena on muodostaa Kauniaisten keskusta-alueen kehittämiselle noin vuoteen 2050 ulottuva yhteinen tavoitetila. Työnsisältö, työvaiheet ja tuotettavat aineistot on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevassa alustavassa työohjelmassa. Hankintaan valitaan yksi (1) toimittaja, jonka kanssa tehdään hankintasopimus. Tarjousten valintaperusteena on kokonaistaloudellisesti edullisin tarjous. Kokonaistaloudellisen edullisuuden vertailuperusteina käytetään hintaa (30 %) ja laatua (70 %). Tarjousten pisteytys sekä laadun arviointiperusteet on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä. Työn arvioitu aloitusajankohta on tammikuu 2027. Sopimuskausi alkaa hankintasopimuksen allekirjoittamisesta ja on voimassa siihen saakka, kunnes toimeksianto on kokonaisuudessaan hyväksytysti toteutettu ja sopimukseen kuuluvat tehtävät onsuoritettu. Tavoitteena on saattaa keskusta-alueen visiotyö valtuustokäsittelyyn vuoden 2028 alussa. Tarjoajan tulee tarjota koko palvelukokonaisuus. Osatarjouksia ei hyväksytä. Hankinnan kokonaisarvon ei arvioida ylittävän hankintalain tarkoittamaa kansallista kynnysarvoa, vaan hankinta on pienhankintana toteutettava palveluhankinta. Hankinta-asiakirjat ovat saatavina täydellisinä ja veloituksetta Cloudian Tarjouspalvelu-toimittajaportaalissa. Mahdolliset hankintaan liittyvät tarkentavat kysymykset tulee lähettää Cloudian Tarjouspalvelu-toimittajaportaalista 15.11.2026 klo 23:59 mennessä. Esitetyistä kysymyksistä ja niihin annetuista vastauksista laaditaan yhteenveto, joka julkaistaan Tarjouspalvelu-toimittajaportaalissa 21.11.2026 mennessä. Kysymykset ja vastaukset esitetään suomen kielellä. Kukin tarjoaja on velvollinen tarkistamaan tarjouspyyntöaineiston ja siihen liittyvät lisätiedot Tarjouspalvelu-toimittajaportaalista ennen tarjouksen jättämistä. Muita lisätietoja ei katsota tilaajaa sitoviksi.

title: Germany – Electrical installation work of heating and other electrical building-equipment – Sanierung Baulich-Technische Infrastruktur: Mess- und Regelungstechnik
description: Die Generalverwaltung des Max Planck Institutes in München soll im laufenden Betrieb umfänglich saniert werden. Inhalt der gemäß Leistungsverzeichnis aufgeführten Leistungen ist die Erbringung von Leistungen der Mess- und Regelungstechnik. Dazu gehören der Aufbau von ASP's zur Regelung und Steuerung von Kälte und Heizungsanlagen. Außerdem ist die Einbindung in den Bestand zu realisieren. Da das Gebäude während der gesamten Arbeiten in Nutzung bleibt, sind alle Tätigkeiten daher mit höchster Sorgfalt sowie unter größtmöglichem Schutz des bestehenden Gebäudes und der vorhandenen Anlagen auszuführen. Um dies umzusetzen läuft das Bauvorhaben in mehreren Bauabschnitten ab. Achtung: Diese Ausschreibung beinhaltet Wartungsleistungen. Ausführungsfristen: Mit der Ausführung ist zu beginnen innerhalb von 12 Werktagen nach Zugang der Aufforderung durch den AG (§5Abs. 2 Satz 2 VOB/B). Die Aufforderung wird Ihnen vorauss. bis zum 01.02.2027 zugehen. Die Leistung ist zu vollenden (abnahmereif fertig zu stellen) innerhalb von 1182 Werktagen nach vorstehend angegebener Frist für den Ausführungsbeginn (5 Arbeitstagen/ Woche) sh. hierzu auch Anlage 1 der Besonderen Vertragsbedingungen VHB-214.. Hinweis betr. Bieterfragen aufgrund besonderer äußerer Ereignisse (z.B. Sars-COV-2 oder Ukraine Krieg): Bitte berücksichtigen Sie bei Ihrer Angebotserstellung etwaige mögliche bzw. erkennbare Beeinträchtigungen, z.B. in Bezug auf die Verfügbarkeit von Materialien und Produkten, Arbeitskräften, eine evtl. verzögerte Beibringung von geforderten Nachweisen, Auswirkungen auf etwaige Nachunternehmer etc. Fragen, die in diesem Zusammenhang auftreten, bitten wir rechtzeitig vor Angebotsfrist über das Nachrichtensystem der eVergabe zu stellen.

title: INDUSTRY DAY: LOW-VOLTAGE ELECTRICAL UPGRADES, VA-WIDE
description: INDUSTRY DAY: LOW-VOLTAGE ELECTRICAL UPGRADES OPPORTUNITIES - VA-WIDE The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Acquisition, Logistics, and Construction (OALC), Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC), is hosting an industry day for vendors interested in providing low-voltage electrical services across multiple VA facilities nationwide. The goal is to share information with vendors about the program and for the government to gauge vendor interest, highlight industry concerns, and assist in the set-aside determination, if any, is appropriate for the program. This is an opportunity for industry to influence procurement decisions that will shape the course of the program. Due to the size, scope and complexity of this initiative, the VA is considering interest from all qualified and interested parties to the industry day event. The event will be a meet and greet, review of scope, deliverables, and review of potential solicitation and award methods. PROJECT DESCRIPTION / DESCRIPTION OF WORK / REQUIREMENT The VA has a requirement for an enterprise-wide program to replace designated existing electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts AC nominal or less, including automatic transfer switches (ATS), transformers, switchgear, and switchboards at more than 100 VA Medical Centers across the country during Fiscal Year 2027. This is a pre-scoped, specification-based, like-for-like equipment replacement program. The Contractor shall provide a completely installed and operational replacement while retaining existing distribution arrangements, feeders, raceways, and associated infrastructure. Work is limited to equipment replacement and necessary incidental installation modifications. EVENT The industry day will be held on December 7, 2026, in Cleveland, OH, from 1:00 PM ET to 4:00 PM ET, at the VA Building located at 6100 Oak Tree Blvd, Independence, OH 44131. Specific meeting room location to be sent to registered attendees. Due to limited accommodations, Registration is required to attend this event and will be limited to a total of 65 attendees and no more than 2 attendees from a firm. Registration will be first come first serve. Additional attendance will be accommodated through a virtual team�s link. title: 13--IL-MIGRATORY BIRD MANAGEMENT-ROCKET NET PROPELLANT
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source IL-Migratory Bird Management- Rocket Net Propellant The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Department of Interior intends to award a firm-fixed price, sole source to Bae Systems Ordnance Systems Inc. pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) part 12.102(a) for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold. This requirement is to provide Rocket Net Propellant under NAICS code 325920 for delivery to Carbondale, IL 62902. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Migratory Bird Management (MBM) has been the facilitator of rocket-net charges and propellant for capturing wildlife and monitoring activities since the 1970s. This program plays a vital role in assessing population trends, migration patterns, and the overall health of wildlife resources. Rocket-net charges require military grade, slow burning propellant with specific performance characteristics necessary to safely deploy nets used for wildlife capture. BAE Systems Ordnance Systems, Inc. is the only known domestic manufacturer capable of producing M6 and PAP-7993 propellant that meets the Government's required military specifications, performance standards, and safety requirements for use in the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service rocket-net wildlife monitoring program. Substitution of alternate propellants would require extensive testing and validation to ensure compatibility with existing rocket-net systems and to verify safe operation during wildlife capture activities. Requirements: � At least 1,000 lbs of M6 or PAP-7993 propellant extruded through 175mm Propelling Charge Dimensions Tooling (F/175mm) with formula and tolerances per MIL-STD-652 (U.S. military standard that defines the chemical, physical, and packing requirements for solid cannon propellants in flake, sheet, or cylindrical grain forms) � Propellant will be packaged in standard fiber drums (United Nations and Department of Transportation packaging code 1G) � Propellant Description Sheets (PDS) and Safety Data Sheets for all lots � Final analysis report for quality assurance � Final production and quality control report documenting manufacturing, inspection, and testing results for delivered lots. Salient characteristics include: � Military-grade slow-burning propellant suitable for rocket-net deployment; � Compatibility with existing USFWS rocket-net systems; � Compliance with applicable military specifications and testing standards; � Demonstrated history of safe performance in wildlife capture operations. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations; however, vendors who feel they can meet this requirement may submit a capability statement. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement. All responses and questions should be directed to Khalilah M. Brown via email at khalilah_brown@ios.doi.gov no later than COB, Wednesday, December 2, 2026. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted.

title: Direct Write Lithography System
description: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory is conducting market research to identify sources that possess the capabilities and experience necessary to provide a direct write lithography system. The LBNL Nanofabrication Facility of the Molecular Foundry is a cleanroom lithographic processing facility specializing in the fabrication of devices with nanoscale features across a variety of microelectronic and quantum materials. The facility consists of 4500 square feet of Class 10 clean room space with environmental control of +/-1oF and +/-2% relative humidity. Process capabilities include deposition of thin films, dry plasma etching, wet chemical etching and cleaning operations, photolithography, electron beam lithography, focus ion beam patterning, and wafer metrology through white light microscopy, ellipsometry, and spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and atomic force microscopy. A new optical lithography system is required to improve reliability, flexibility and turnaround time to speed up R&D cycles. Please see the attached RFI document for desired specifications and response instructions.

title: INDUSTRY DAY: LOW-VOLTAGE ELECTRICAL UPGRADES, VA-WIDE
description: INDUSTRY DAY: LOW-VOLTAGE ELECTRICAL UPGRADES OPPORTUNITIES - VA-WIDE The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Acquisition, Logistics, and Construction (OALC), Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC), is hosting an industry day for vendors interested in providing low-voltage electrical services across multiple VA facilities nationwide. The goal is to share information with vendors about the program and for the government to gauge vendor interest, highlight industry concerns, and assist in the set-aside determination, if any, is appropriate for the program. This is an opportunity for industry to influence procurement decisions that will shape the course of the program. Due to the size, scope and complexity of this initiative, the VA is considering interest from all qualified and interested parties to the industry day event. The event will be a meet and greet, review of scope, deliverables, and review of potential solicitation and award methods. This is a pre-scoped, specification-based, like-for-like equipment replacement program. The Contractor shall provide a completely installed and operational replacement while retaining existing distribution arrangements, feeders, raceways, and associated infrastructure. Work is limited to equipment replacement and necessary incidental installation modifications. title: 13--IL-MIGRATORY BIRD MANAGEMENT-ROCKET NET PROPELLANT
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source IL-Migratory Bird Management- Rocket Net Propellant The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Department of Interior intends to award a firm-fixed price, sole source to Bae Systems Ordnance Systems Inc. pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) part 12.102(a) for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold. This requirement is to provide Rocket Net Propellant under NAICS code 325920 for delivery to Carbondale, IL 62902. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Migratory Bird Management (MBM) has been the facilitator of rocket-net charges and propellant for capturing wildlife and monitoring activities since the 1970s. This program plays a vital role in assessing population trends, migration patterns, and the overall health of wildlife resources. Rocket-net charges require military grade, slow burning propellant with specific performance characteristics necessary to safely deploy nets used for wildlife capture. BAE Systems Ordnance Systems, Inc. is the only known domestic manufacturer capable of producing M6 and PAP-7993 propellant that meets the Government's required military specifications, performance standards, and safety requirements for use in the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service rocket-net wildlife monitoring program. Substitution of alternate propellants would require extensive testing and validation to ensure compatibility with existing rocket-net systems and to verify safe operation during wildlife capture activities. Requirements: - At least 1,000 lbs of M6 or PAP-7993 propellant extruded through 175mm Propelling Charge Dimensions Tooling (F/175mm) with formula and tolerances per MIL-STD-652 (U.S. military standard that defines the chemical, physical, and packing requirements for solid cannon propellants in flake, sheet, or cylindrical grain forms) - Propellant will be packaged in standard fiber drums (United Nations and Department of Transportation packaging code 1G) - Propellant Description Sheets (PDS) and Safety Data Sheets for all lots - Final analysis report for quality assurance - Final production and quality control report documenting manufacturing, inspection, and testing results for delivered lots. Salient characteristics include: - Military-grade slow-burning propellant suitable for rocket-net deployment; - Compatibility with existing USFWS rocket-net systems; - Compliance with applicable military specifications and testing standards; - Demonstrated history of safe performance in wildlife capture operations. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations; however, vendors who feel they can meet this requirement may submit a capability statement. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement. All responses and questions should be directed to Khalilah M. Brown via email at khalilah_brown@ios.doi.gov no later than COB, Wednesday, December 2, 2026. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted.

description: INDUSTRY DAY: LOW-VOLTAGE ELECTRICAL UPGRADES OPPORTUNITIES - VA-WIDE The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Acquisition, Logistics, and Construction (OALC), Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC), is hosting an industry day for vendors interested in providing low-voltage electrical services across multiple VA facilities nationwide. The goal is to share information with vendors about the program and for the government to gauge vendor interest, highlight industry concerns, and assist in the set-aside determination, if any, is appropriate for the program. This is an opportunity for industry to influence procurement decisions that will shape the course of the program. Due to the size, scope and complexity of this initiative, the VA is considering interest from all qualified and interested parties to the industry day event. The event will be a meet and greet, review of scope, deliverables, and review of potential solicitation and award methods. PROJECT DESCRIPTION / DESCRIPTION OF WORK / REQUIREMENT The VA has a requirement for an enterprise-wide program to replace designated existing electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts AC nominal or less, including automatic transfer switches (ATS), transformers, switchgear, and switchboards at more than 100 VA Medical Centers across the country during Fiscal Year 2027. This is a pre-scoped, specification-based, like-for-like equipment replacement program. The Contractor shall provide a completely installed and operational replacement while retaining existing distribution arrangements, feeders, raceways, and associated infrastructure. Work is limited to equipment replacement and necessary incidental installation modifications. title: 8910 - Dairy Products and Refrigerated Delivery � VA Sierra Nevada Health Care System
description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE Dairy Products and Refrigerated Delivery � VA Sierra Nevada Health Care System PURPOSE The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Regional Procurement Office West (RPOW), Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 5, Health Service Area (HSA) 5.2, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 21, on behalf of VA Sierra Nevada Health Care System (VASNHCS), is conducting market research to identify businesses capable of supplying and delivering fresh dairy products for Veteran patient meal services. DESCRIPTION OF ANTICIPATED REQUIREMENT The contractor would furnish the products, labor, refrigerated transportation, delivery equipment, and associated resources necessary to supply and deliver pasteurized milk and other dairy products to the facility located at 975 Kirman Avenue, Building 1C, Reno, NV 89502 at least twice a week. The requirement is defined by product characteristics, freshness, food safety, and delivery performance, rather than a particular brand, manufacturer, or distributor. The prospective contractor would provide the following descriptions and estimated annual quantities: Item 1: Pasteurized 2% reduced-fat milk; half-gallon container; reference pack 12 containers per case; estimated annual quantity 1,000 containers. Item 2: Pasteurized whole milk; half-pint (8-fluid-ounce) individual container; reference pack 70 containers per case; estimated annual quantity 9,500 containers. Item 3: Pasteurized 1% lowfat milk; half-pint (8-fluid-ounce) individual container; reference pack 70 containers per case; estimated annual quantity 43,000 containers. DELIVERY AND QUALITY EXPECTATIONS Anticipated deliveries are twice weekly, Tuesday and Friday, between 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. local Reno time, to the address above. Holiday adjustments would be coordinated in advance. Deliveries would include contractor unloading and movement to the designated receiving point in the presence of authorized VA personnel. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT STRUCTURE The Government anticipates an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) supply contract with firm-fixed unit prices and delivery orders issued as needs arise. A 12-month base ordering period and four 12-month option ordering periods are contemplated, subject to confirmation. Contract dates, minimum guarantee, maximum quantity or value, order limitations, and final award structure have not been established and will be stated in any resulting solicitation. description: Sources Sought Notice Spectrum Engineering Technical Support Services for the Navy and Marine Corps Spectrum Center (NMSC) This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is in anticipation of a potential future procurement under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541330, Engineering Services. Subject to FAR 15.101, entitled Early Exchanges with Industry, this announcement constitutes an SSN for written information only. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals, and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. This SSN is not to be construed in any way as a commitment by the U.S. Government, nor will the U.S. Government pay for the information submitted in response. Failure to respond to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotation (RFQ), should one be issued. In the event a solicitation is released in the future, it will be posted to the Governmentwide Point of Entry at SAM.gov. Potential offerors/quoters are responsible for monitoring the site for updates and additional information regarding this requirement. 1. Description The Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Norfolk Contracting Department is seeking information from interested sources capable of providing Spectrum Engineering and Technical Support Services in support of the Navy and Marine Corps Spectrum Center (NMSC). The requirement includes specialized engineering, analytical, software development and sustainment, and administrative support associated with electromagnetic spectrum management, spectrum certification, electromagnetic compatibility, and national security missions. The specific acquisition strategy has not yet been finalized. Interested parties are encouraged to review the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), which outlines the types of tasks the contractor would be required to perform. 2. Requirements The Government is conducting market research to determine the availability and capabilities of potential sources, including small businesses, to perform the requirements described in the attached draft PWS. The anticipated services include, but are not limited to: Spectrum engineering, certification, and electromagnetic compatibility analysis. Satellite spectrum engineering and coordination. Engineering support for commercial broadband installations and spectrum-sharing initiatives. Joint Tactical Information Distribution System (JTIDS), Multifunctional Information Distribution System (MIDS), and Joint Tactical Radio System (JTRS) engineering and coordination. Electromagnetic Compatibility Features (EMCF) certification and validation. Link 16 Pulse Deconfliction Server (LPDS) administration, software development, maintenance, sustainment, and cybersecurity support. Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) engineering, research, development, test, and evaluation support. Spectrum supportability risk assessments, acquisition program support, and national spectrum policy analysis. Specialized administrative and technical coordination support. The Government has determined that these services qualify as commercial services, as defined in FAR 2.101. If solicited, it is anticipated that this requirement will fall under NAICS codes 541330, with a small business size standard of $25.5 million. The anticipated Product/Service Code (PSC) is R425 � Support: Professional � Engineering/Technical. The draft PWS identifies performance primarily within the National Capital Region, including Government facilities at Fort Meade, Maryland, and contractor-provided locations. The requirement also includes travel to other locations as necessary. Personnel performing the requirement must meet the security clearance requirements specified in the draft PWS, including Secret-level eligibility and adjudication at contract start, with certain positions potentially requiring higher-level clearances. The Government has not yet finalized the acquisition vehicle, contract type, or small business set-aside determination, if any. 3. Capability Statements This is a market research tool. The input provided will help the Government ascertain the interest, capability, and capacity of potential contractors. Standard company brochures will not be reviewed. Submission must not exceed five (5) typewritten pages including cover sheet, using no less than a 10-point font size. Responses should be emailed to Dave Vaughn (david.e.vaughn6.civ@us.navy.mil) and Amber Geusic (amber.m.geusic.civ@us.navy.mil) no later than 05:00 PM EST on 02 December 2026. Technical questions and inquiries may be submitted along with the response; however, the Government is not obligated to answer any questions submitted regarding this SSN. Please note that the information contained in this SSN is for informational purposes only and is subject to change prior to the issuance of any formal solicitation, if one is issued at all. Small Business Category, if any: Small Business, Small Disadvantaged, 8(a), HUBZone, Woman-owned, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, or other category. All currently held contracting vehicles under which the vendor can provide the required services (ex. GSA, SEWP, SeaPort-NxG). Standard brochures and/or paraphrasing of the SSN will not be considered sufficient to demonstrate capability. Address the respondent�s experience with electromagnetic spectrum engineering, spectrum certification, electromagnetic compatibility, and military communications systems, including Link 16 and related technologies. Describe the respondent�s capabilities in software development, sustainment, cybersecurity, and administration of specialized Government information systems, particularly those involving spectrum management or deconfliction. Explain the respondent�s ability to provide appropriately qualified and cleared personnel to meet the technical, administrative, and security requirements of the draft PWS. If providing past performance information, contracts or efforts must be from within the past five (5) years. The discussion must include the applicable contract or task order number and contract vehicle, clearly indicate whether the respondent was a prime contractor or subcontractor under the effort, and provide the final contract price, dates of performance, and project location. Include a brief description of the effort along with a detailed explanation demonstrating its relevance to the requirements in the PWS. 4. Industry Discussions NAVSUP FLC Norfolk Contracting Department representatives may or may not choose to meet with respondents. Any discussions would be solely for the purpose of obtaining further clarification regarding a respondent�s capability to meet the requirements. 5. Questions Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted directly to Dave Vaughn (david.e.vaughn6.civ@us.navy.mil) and Amber Geusic (amber.m.geusic.civ@us.navy.mil) by 02 December 2026. title: Market Research / Sources Sought � Engineered Cable Support Systems
description: Notice of intent to use a brand name product. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Pacific (NAVFAC Pacific) is conducting market research in accordance with FAR Part 10 to identify potential manufacturers capable of producing engineered cable support systems that have equal performance and listing/approval requirements as the E-loop engineered cable support system that is manufactured by Igus. Responses from third-party distributors, pass through resellers, or supply brokers who do not directly own the production line or manufacturing rights to a qualified equivalent product will not be considered responsive to this market survey. FY27 MCON Project P-676 Polaris Point Submarine Pier, located Naval Base Guam requires engineered cable support systems that demonstrate the following salient characteristics: System ensures the seamless transition of electrical and telecom cables from landside to the pier. The pier structure is expected to experience up to 24 inches of displacement during a contingency level earthquake (CLE). Therefore, the electrical and telecom cables must be able to displace, expand, and contract in response to these seismic movements. Typical conduit expansion and deflection fittings allow for only limited movement, accommodating just a few inches of angular and horizontal movement, making them unsuitable for this application. Allows electrical and telecom cables to be sized for plus/minus 36 inches of pier movement, exceeding the expected displacement during a CLE. System will provide strain relief and allow the cables to move during a seismic event without going below the cable's minimum bending radius. Also, the type of cable used remains consistent without compromising its properties, despite concerns about potential damage from seismic activity. This is not a request for proposals, quotes, or an invitation for bid. The intent of this notice is to identify potential alternative engineered cable support systems that will satisfy agency requirements. To be considered, please submit detailed technical data in order for the Government to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of your product to ensure compatibility with the existing system. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c)(2), a response to this notice is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The responder is solely responsible for the information it submits and any associated costs. The Government reserves the right to disregard any submittal that is incomplete or vague. Please do not submit company brochures. Please submit complete information via email to Ms. Michelle Gopwani-Lee via electronic mail at michelle.m.gopwani-lee.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 02 December 2026 at 12:30 p.m. H.S.T. Information received after the due date/time will not be considered. Any information provided to the Government in response to this RFI will become U.S. Government property and will not be returned. All proprietary or classified information will be treated appropriately.
